Regarding regional dynamics, the analysis considers landscape changes driven by wet and dry seasons, land management practices (such as native pasture clearing, cattle grazing, and the use of fire), the replacement of native grasslands with exotic pastures, and the classification of wetlands (temporary ponds, floodplains, and drainage channels) within the mapped Vegetation Loss polygons.

title: Object Detection in Small-Sample Underwater Sonar Images Using Improved YOLOv11
summary: Underwater object detection in sonar images is challenging because of low image resolution, acoustic noise, seabed clutter, weak target boundaries, substantial target-scale variation, and limited labeled data. To address these challenges, we develop an improved You Only Look Once version 11 (YOLOv11)-based framework for small-sample sonar object detection. Rather than introducing new individual network components, the proposed framework coordinates hierarchical feature extraction, local contextual feature processing, and scale-adaptive detection according to the characteristics of sonar imagery. Specifically, a ResNet50 backbone is used to obtain deeper multilevel representations, a RepViT-enhanced C3k2 module is incorporated to strengthen the representation of small and low-contrast targets in cluttered backgrounds, a dual-pooling operation is employed to preserve prominent local echo responses and broader contextual information, and Dynamic Head is used to improve feature aggregation across different target scales and spatial locations. In addition, data augmentation and image synthesis techniques are applied to increase sample diversity and mitigate overfitting under limited-data conditions. Experiments on the Sonar Object Detection (SOD) and Underwater Acoustic Target Detection (UATD) datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. On the SOD dataset, the model achieves an F1-score of 92.61%, an mAP@0.5 of 77.4%, and an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 59.3%. On the UATD dataset, it achieves an F1-score of 84.0%, an mAP@0.5 of 85.1%, and an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 38.1%. The experimental results confirm the model’s robustness in challenging underwater scenarios and its strong potential for high-precision applications in oceanic exploration, maritime rescue, and surveillance.

title: WTC-CNXGRN: An Operational Wind Turbine Clutter Detection Model for Dual-Polarization Radar Under Complex Weather
summary: Wind turbine clutter (WTC) can severely degrade the quality of meteorological radar data, particularly under complex weather conditions. Because WTC echoes can substantially overlap with precipitation echoes, they may introduce considerable errors into weather identification and forecasting. To address this issue, a deep learning model termed WTC-CNXGRN is proposed for automatic WTC detection. The model is built on the ConvNeXtV2 architecture and is designed to address characteristic WTC features, including unstable spatial structure, pronounced local texture variations, and complex multi-channel feature coupling. Multi-parameter dual-polarization weather radar data are used as input, while local statistical features and weighted polarimetric features are incorporated to strengthen the representation of spatial echo variations. In addition, a Global Response Normalization (GRN) mechanism is integrated into the network to adaptively recalibrate channel-wise responses, thereby enhancing the representation of critical discriminative features. On the test dataset, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 98.74%, a precision of 98.41%, a probability of detection (POD) of 98.34%, and a false alarm ratio (FAR) of 1.59%, achieving overall better performance than the evaluated baseline models. Benefiting from its efficient architecture and improved detection strategy, the model provides low computational cost and fast inference, making it suitable for near-real-time operational applications. Qualitative tests using radar data from the Nantong region further provide preliminary evidence of the model’s cross-site applicability.

title: SAGE: Shadow-Adaptive Geometric Supervision for Earth Observation Gaussian Splatting
summary: Accurate reconstruction of digital surface models (DSMs) from multi-date high-resolution urban satellite imagery supports large-scale Earth observation and three-dimensional city modeling, with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) emerging as an efficient solution. Existing shadow-aware methods provide shadow-related spatial evidence, whereas geometric priors are generally applied across the image or scene without using this evidence to allocate supervision. Consequently, regions where shadows overlap abrupt elevation transitions may remain geometrically under-constrained, producing spatially non-uniform elevation errors whose severity varies with the geometry covered by shadow. To address this issue, we propose Shadow-Adaptive Geometric Supervision for Earth Observation Gaussian Splatting (SAGE). SAGE is primarily designed for urban scenes dominated by regular human-made structures and retains image-wide altitude guidance while allocating additional geometric supervision at two levels. At the spatial level, patch-level shadow weights determine where a shadow-targeted local altitude prior is applied to constrain relative altitude agreement. At the scene level, SAGE computes the reconstruction-derived Shadow Geometric Complexity (SGC) from multi-view shadow evidence and gradient statistics of the predicted DSM. SGC is used as a scene-level descriptor of shadow–gradient contrast and determines how strongly the local altitude prior and the complementary Manhattan orientation regularization are applied. Experiments on seven predominantly urban scenes from the DFC2019 and IARPA 2016 benchmarks show that SAGE achieves the best mean DSM accuracy on both benchmarks while retaining minute-level processing.

title: Subglacial Radar Reflectivity Estimation Considering Volumetric Scattering Loss from Englacial Dielectric Inhomogeneities
summary: To improve the accuracy of subglacial reflectivity estimation using ice-sounding radar, this study proposes a method that explicitly incorporates volumetric scattering loss caused by englacial dielectric inhomogeneities. Particle scattering from englacial dielectric inhomogeneities is accounted for using Rayleigh and Mie theory, with the applicable formulation selected according to the relationship between the characteristic size of the inhomogeneities and the radar wavelength. The resulting scattering loss is incorporated into the conventional propagation-loss model to obtain corrected basal reflectivity estimates. Main simulations of bedrock–subglacial water and bedrock–sediment transitions were conducted at a center frequency of 200 MHz using an effective scatterer radius of 0.2 mm and porosities of 0.5% and 0.8%. Supplementary simulations were further performed at 60 MHz, corresponding to the operating frequency of the airborne radar system used in the field experiments. Compared with the conventional attenuation-correction method, the proposed method produced reflectivity estimates closer to the prescribed reference values and reduced the RMSE by approximately 29.2–34.8%. The method was further validated using airborne radar data from Lake Snow Eagle, Lake Vostok, the Lambert Glacier Basin, and Dome A. At Lake Vostok, the absolute deviation from the reference value was reduced from 0.85 to 0.47 dB, while at Dome A it was reduced from 1.01 to 0.71 dB. These results demonstrate that explicitly accounting for volumetric scattering loss can reduce systematic reflectivity bias and improve the accuracy and reliability of subglacial water, sediment, and bedrock characterization.

title: A Structure-Aware Semantic Prototype Constraint Network for Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
summary: Remote sensing images are critical for extracting land surface information, supporting land-use planning and ecological protection. While remote sensing image segmentation automatically identifies target regions within complex scenes, existing methods often fail to balance semantic discrimination with boundary recovery due to intricate object morphologies and blurred edges. To address this challenge, this study introduces SSPCNet, a structure-aware semantic prototype-constrained network designed to enhance target recognition. SSPCNet introduces a structure-aware feature representation strategy to enhance the extraction of local textures, directional structures, and boundary-sensitive information, thereby improving the perception of complex object geometries. Furthermore, a semantic prototype-constrained decoder is developed to establish cross-layer semantic consistency by introducing shared semantic prototypes and prototype-constrained feature interaction, enabling effective integration of hierarchical features and improving the recognition of densely and sparsely distributed targets. Evaluated against eight representative segmentation methods across four public datasets using three independent runs with different random seeds, SSPCNet demonstrates strong and consistent performance. Notably, on the ISPRS Potsdam dataset, SSPCNet achieves an ACC of 85.23 ± 0.96%, an mIoU of 70.60 ± 1.40%, and a Harmonic Mean of 82.00 ± 1.01%, while requiring only 14.40 GFLOPs and 6.24 M parameters, demonstrating a favorable balance between segmentation performance and model complexity for remote sensing image interpretation.

title: Atmospheric Relief vs. Hydrological Buffering: How Changing Precipitation Characteristics Regulate Gross Primary Productivity in Central Asian Drylands
summary: Global-warming-induced shifts in precipitation regimes profoundly affect terrestrial vegetation productivity; however, the pathways through which precipitation characteristics regulate gross primary productivity (GPP) remain insufficiently understood. Using meteorological records, satellite remote-sensing products, and reanalysis data from 2000 to 2024, we quantified GPP responses to changing precipitation regimes in Central Asian drylands through superposed epoch analysis, random forest and TreeSHAP analyses, and cross-lagged structural equation modeling (CB-SEM). Against a background of increasing annual precipitation (1.79 mm yr−1, p = 0.014), synchronous increases in precipitation frequency and intensity enhanced dryland productivity, with increasing GPP (0.28 g C m−2 yr−1, p = 0.726). The two precipitation-frequency metrics increased across 75.10–82.46% of the study area, whereas the intensity metrics increased across 64.16–81.67%. Frequent precipitation rapidly reduced vapor pressure deficit (VPD) and maintained shallow soil moisture, producing GPP anomaly gains ~0.5 g C m−2 8 d−1 across extensive Central Asian plains. In contrast, high-intensity precipitation replenished deep soil moisture and sustained GPP anomaly gains of 0.5–1.5 g C m−2 8 d−1 in the semi-arid steppe of northern Kazakhstan. CB-SEM identified VPD as the strongest direct climatic driver of GPP (−0.482), followed by soil moisture (0.290) and temperature (0.283). Precipitation frequency directly reduced VPD (−0.016), whereas precipitation intensity positively affected soil moisture (0.057). The frequency-mediated atmospheric pathway was strongest during the initial t (0–8-day) response period, while the intensity-mediated soil-moisture pathway became increasingly important after 8 days. These findings reveal complementary atmospheric-regulation and soil-moisture-buffering mechanisms and provide a process-based framework for improving the representation of dryland carbon–water coupling under changing precipitation regimes.

title: LTGC-Diff: A Local-Token and Global-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Model for SAR-Assisted Remote Sensing Image Cloud Removal
summary: Cloud contamination in optical remote sensing imagery can obscure land-surface information and induce structural blurring and spectral shifts, thereby seriously affecting subsequent land-cover interpretation and quantitative analysis. To address the instability of optical image restoration under complex cloud occlusion and the difficulty of effectively exploiting SAR auxiliary information, this paper proposes LTGC-Diff, a latent diffusion model for SAR-assisted remote sensing image cloud removal. The proposed method formulates cloud-free RGB image restoration as a latent denoising process constrained by multi-source observations. To better incorporate SAR auxiliary information into diffusion reconstruction, a diffusion-oriented conditional representation learning module is designed to transform SAR-derived features into effective conditional representations. In addition, a token-level structural condition adaptation module is designed to transform SAR patch representations into local structural guidance suitable for diffusion-based reconstruction. By jointly exploiting global scene-level guidance and local structure-aware constraints, the proposed model enables more stable and reliable recovery of cloud-obscured regions. Experimental results demonstrate that LTGC-Diff improves the structural consistency and restoration reliability of SAR-assisted optical remote sensing image cloud removal under complex cloud-contaminated scenarios. Specifically, LTGC-Diff achieves a PSNR of 32.87 dB while maintaining improved structural and spectral consistency, demonstrating its effectiveness for SAR-assisted cloud removal.

title: Ecological Indicators Reveal Contrasting Post-Earthquake Recovery Trajectories and Resilience Across Mountain Ecosystems
summary: Net primary productivity (NPP) is a useful ecological indicator for evaluating ecosystem functioning and recovery after natural disturbance. Here, we used multi-source remote-sensing and environmental data from 2010 to 2024 to compare post-earthquake NPP recovery in the 2017 Jiuzhaigou and Milin earthquake regions. We integrated trend analysis, temporal persistence assessment, co-seismic landslide overlay, eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and locally weighted scatterplot smoothing (LOWESS)-based contribution-transition detection to compare NPP dynamics and environmental associations in the two earthquake-affected regions. The two regions exhibited contrasting responses. The slope of regional mean annual NPP decreased from 9.69 to 8.21 g C m−2 yr−2 between the pre- and post-earthquake periods in Jiuzhaigou, whereas it increased from 3.69 to 9.37 g C m−2 yr−2 in Milin. Hurst-based trend-persistence analysis indicated a higher proportion of sustained improvement and a lower proportion of degradation-related classes in Jiuzhaigou, whereas Milin showed more degradation-related classes. Within co-seismic landslide zones, sustained degradation dominated in both regions and was more extensive in Milin. XGBoost–SHAP results showed that pre-earthquake NPP was the most influential predictor in both regions, but the contributions of secondary predictors differed. Elevation made a larger relative contribution to the Jiuzhaigou model, whereas pre-earthquake NDVI, precipitation, and temperature made larger relative contributions to the Milin model. LOWESS analysis further revealed distinct nonlinear response transitions in temperature, precipitation, and elevation. These results demonstrate the value of combining NPP trends, temporal persistence, and model interpretation to compare vegetation productivity dynamics and inform assessments of post-earthquake functional recovery in mountain ecosystems.

title: Laser-Induced Fluorescence Hyperspectral Imaging for Classification of Coastal Macroalgae, Eelgrass, and Mussels
summary: This study explores the application of fluorescence hyperspectral imaging (FHSI) for marine ecosystem monitoring, combining laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) with hyperspectral imaging (HSI), an approach rarely applied in marine ecology. Photopigments such as chlorophylls, carotenoids, and phycobiliproteins emit distinct fluorescence signals when excited at specific wavelengths. Species-discriminating spectral signatures can then address persistent challenges in benthic monitoring, including overlapping optical properties among species and complex underwater conditions. Using a cheap 450 nm broad area diode laser, a push-broom hyperspectral camera, and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), we classified brown, red, and green macroalgae, eelgrass, and blue mussels in laboratory and field experiments in Danish coastal waters, achieving macro-F1 scores of 80% and 85%, respectively. We show that the method was highly accurate for photopigmented organisms but limited for dark-coloured, low-fluorescence species such as mussels. Field deployment further showed that ambient sunlight and water turbidity are the dominant constraints on in-situ performance, and that including laser reflectance as an additional spectral feature improved classification under natural illumination. These findings establish FHSI as a promising tool for automated benthic habitat analysis and remote-sensing-based marine ecosystem monitoring.

title: Enhancing FY-3E/VASS Humidity Profiles During a Cloudy Atmospheric River Event Using Clear-Sky FY-4B/GIIRS Guidance
summary: Atmospheric rivers (ARs) are characterized by high water vapor content and are frequently accompanied by extensive cloud cover, creating a need for reliable humidity profiles under cloudy conditions. Fengyun-4B/Geostationary Interferometric Infrared Sounder (FY-4B/GIIRS) products provide relatively accurate clear-sky humidity profiles, whereas Fengyun-3E/Vertical Atmospheric Sounding System (FY-3E/VASS) products offer all-sky coverage but retain appreciable humidity errors. This study develops a clear-sky FY-4B/GIIRS-guided framework to enhance cloudy-sky FY-3E/VASS humidity profiles. Spatiotemporally collocated clear-sky profiles are first used to construct humidity residuals, from which principal component analysis extracts a low-dimensional residual basis. A neural network then predicts the corresponding coefficients to generate a baseline correction. Target-day calibration and cloud-condition adjustment further adapt this clear-sky-derived correction to cloudy-sky samples on the target day. The framework is evaluated against ERA5 reanalysis for a preidentified AR event along the eastern coast of China on 6 July 2023, using cloudy-sky samples from the 09:31–09:41 UTC FY-3E overpass. For all cloudy-sky samples from this overpass, the pressure-level-averaged root mean square error (RMSE) decreases by 16.1% over 300–900 hPa and by 20.8% over 700–900 hPa. For cloudy-sky samples in the high-moisture AR subset, the corresponding reductions are 19.7% and 26.6%, respectively. The overlap between the high-moisture masks defined using integrated water vapor (IWV) from FY-3E/VASS and ERA5 increases from 60.7% to 73.9%. The enhanced profiles therefore show improved agreement with ERA5, particularly over 700–900 hPa, and better represent the high-moisture portion of the examined AR event.

title: ISODATA Clustering Approach for Mapping and Characterization of Surface Urban Heat Island Intensities Using Time Series of Remotely Sensed Land Surface Temperature and Land-Use/Land-Cover Products
summary: This study evaluated spatial patterns and trends in surface urban heat island intensities (SUHIIs) across three major cities in Alabama, USA: Huntsville, Birmingham, and Mobile. Spatial expansion of developed areas and magnitudes and trends of SUHIs were mapped and quantified using land-use/land-cover (LULC) data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) and land-surface temperature (LST) products from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), respectively. Our findings reveal urban expansion over all three study areas, but at varying rates and patterns. The ISODATA clustering approach using time series of LST data was able to map surface urban heat islands (SUHIs) as distinguished clusters of significantly (p=0.01) warmer surface temperatures as compared to their surroundings. Spatial distributions of the SUHI clusters over all three cities closely resembled spatial distributions of the developed areas. Our findings also revealed significantly different SUHI intensities (p=0.05) among the three study areas (during day and nighttime of summer and winter seasons). These findings indicate the ISODATA clustering approach using time series of satellite-derived LST products as a promising approach for local-scale mapping and characterization of SUHIs. Our findings also provide detailed insights for improved understanding of the spatial distributions and temporal variations of SUHI developments.

title: Ellipse-ABC: An Efficient Geometry-Consistent Quadratic Representation for Oriented Object Detection in Remote-Sensing Images
summary: Oriented object detection in remote-sensing imagery benefits from a geometric representation that remains well-defined across localization, label assignment, and post-processing. We present Ellipse-ABC, a YOLOv8-based detector that directly predicts the coefficients of a positive-definite quadratic form while retaining the original branch for center estimation. The resulting matrix supplies Gaussian-compatible localization supervision and is analytically decoded into standardized OBB geometry for task-aligned assignment, rotated non-maximum suppression, and benchmark reporting, thereby reducing representation changes across the pipeline. Primary accuracy is evaluated with polygon area IoU between predicted and ground-truth-oriented bounding boxes. After rerunning the native baseline under the same dataset-specific training and augmentation recipes used by the ABC configurations, the complete ABC + GWD configuration changes polygon-IoU mAP50/mAP50-95 by +2.16/−1.17 points on UCAS-AOD and −1.23/+0.50 points on HRSC2016 across seeds 0, 1, and 2. An ABC + ProbIoU loss control performs better than ABC + GWD on HRSC2016 but worse on UCAS-AOD, indicating that the geometry-loss choice is dataset-dependent. The representation adds 198 parameters and no more than 0.0018 GFLOPs at the evaluated input sizes. Five repeated batch-1 measurements nevertheless show a 6.6–8.8% end-to-end latency increase and higher peak memory on DOTA-v1.5. These results support Ellipse-ABC as a geometry-consistent representation with small model-level overhead, without implying a universal accuracy gain.

title: Normality-Calibrated Modality Routing for Optical-SAR Object Detection Under Cloud-Induced Optical Degradation
summary: Optical-SAR object detectors trained on cloud-free paired imagery tend to develop a strong dependence on the information-rich optical modality. Consequently, the availability of SAR observations does not necessarily guarantee their effective use when optical information becomes unreliable under cloud occlusion. To address this issue, we propose NCMR-Net, a Normality-Calibrated Modality Routing Network that enables spatially adaptive optical-to-SAR routing without image-level cloud augmentation. NCMR-Net retains the standard YOLOv11s detection architecture and introduces three functional modules along the optical-SAR interaction and routing pathway. First, the Frequency-Selective SAR Refinement (FSR) module applies Haar-based subband decomposition and bounded high-frequency correction to construct a more usable SAR fallback representation. Second, the Normality-Calibrated Gating (NCG) module derives non-learnable input-domain evidence from high brightness and reduced local texture, which characterize the optical information collapse associated with cloud degradation. NCG calibrates this evidence against its empirical distribution under normal optical observations. At inference, a lower bound on the SAR mixing coefficient maintains optical-SAR fusion at low NCG responses, while stronger responses increase the SAR coefficient above this bound. Finally, the Gate-Conditioned Residual Adaptation (GCRA) module combines the routing gate with local feature statistics and performs gate-conditioned, identity-initialized residual adaptation across different routing states. In the single-run OSPRC evaluation, NCMR-Net is trained on cloud-free RGB10M-VH pairs without image-level cloud augmentation. Under the matched RGB10M-VH condition, NCMR-Net achieves 85.12%mAP50 and 53.57%mAP50:95, compared with 83.48% and 53.30% for YOLOv11s-Add. Without retraining, fine-tuning, or test-time adaptation, it achieves 64.48%mAP50 under the synthetic cloud-degraded CLUDE-VH condition, exceeding the baseline’s 39.15% by 25.33 percentage points. The corresponding mAP50 retention rates are 75.8% for NCMR-Net and 46.9% for YOLOv11s-Add. These results support improved performance retention under the tested synthetic cloud degradation; generalization to real clouds remains to be established.

title: TPA-NET: A Progressive Cross-Modal Alignment and Confidence Fusion Network for Object Detection in Low-Resolution Optical-SAR Remote Sensing Imagery
summary: Object detection in low-resolution optical-SAR remote sensing imagery is challenged by degraded object structures, residual cross-modal spatial inconsistency, and unreliable SAR responses. To address these issues, we propose TPA-NET, a progressive cross-modal alignment and confidence fusion network built on YOLOv10. TPA-NET adopts a three-stage coarse-to-fine processing strategy. The Shallow Coarse Alignment (SCA) module performs initial feature-space calibration, the Pyramid Residual Alignment (PRA) module further refines local cross-modal correspondence across multiple scales, and the Detection-aware Confidence Fusion (DCF) module dynamically regulates modality contributions according to object responses and task-driven feature reliability. The framework is trained end-to-end without additional image-level registration or manual correction. Experimental results show that TPA-NET achieves 95.4% mAP50 and 71.4% mAP50–95 on OGSOD 1.0, improving mAP50–95 by 1.9 percentage points over IRDFusion. On M4-SAR, it achieves 86.1% mAP50 and 62.0% mAP50–95, exceeding E2E-OSDet by 0.5 and 0.8 percentage points, respectively. Ablation and visualization analyses further support the effectiveness of progressive feature calibration and reliability-aware fusion for improving cross-modal object localization.

title: Correlational Mode Reconstruction Method for Maritime Radar Target Detection
summary: Under strong sea clutter conditions, radar echoes from moving sea-surface targets are easily masked by background clutter. A major limitation of existing mode decomposition and reconstruction approaches is the difficulty in reliably distinguishing target-related modes. To address this challenge, a radar target feature detection method based on Correlational Mode Reconstruction is proposed. The original radar signal is first decomposed into a set of intrinsic mode functions using Variational Mode Decomposition. An ideal target reference model is then constructed by combining time–frequency analysis with morphological image processing. A multi-dimensional correlation metric is then developed to evaluate the degree of match between each mode and the model signal, enabling accurate selection of target modes. Features are subsequently extracted from the reconstructed signal in multiple transform domains, and a relative feature gain metric is used to select discriminative features. The experimental results demonstrate that, irrespective of the feature-based detector used, the proposed reconstruction provides better detection performance than the original signals and the other reconstruction strategies. In addition, feature fusion further improves detection performance over single feature detection.

title: A Practical Fixed-Configuration, Training-Free Baseline for Within-Sensor Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection
summary: Hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD) aims to identify rare targets without labeled anomaly samples, but many recent deep HAD approaches require scene-specific neural optimization, increasing deployment cost. This paper presents MASCR-UAF, a fixed-configuration baseline designed for training-free within-sensor HAD. Global hyperparameters are calibrated on a designated calibration split and frozen before evaluation. No target-scene labels, neural-network retraining, gradient-based adaptation, or target-label-based hyperparameter selection are used, although unlabeled statistical quantities are estimated independently from each test scene following classical HAD conventions. MASCR-UAF integrates complementary spectral, density, and spatial anomaly cues through an unsupervised adaptive fusion rule. On ten held-out AVIRIS ABU scenes, the framework achieves competitive AUC-ROC performance while providing improved AUC-PR and low-false-alarm operating characteristics compared with the evaluated individual statistical detectors. Additional evaluations on Indian Pines, San Diego, and Pavia University reveal regime-dependent behavior across agricultural, airport, and sensor conditions. These results suggest that MASCR-UAF can serve as a practical reference for within-sensor cross-scene HAD, while its applicability beyond this setting requires further investigation.

title: DSFormer: An Enhanced Dual-Selective Fusion Transformer Framework for Hyperspectral Image Classification++
summary: Hyperspectral image classification requires joint modeling of spectral signatures and spatial structure. In patch-based classification, each input patch is assigned the label of its center pixel, although neighboring pixels may belong to different land-cover classes. This setting motivates coordinating shallow spatial features, contextual refinement within the patch, and supervision of the resulting representation. We propose DSFormer++, an enhanced framework based on the original Dual Selective Fusion Transformer Network (DSFormer). Shallow Feature Compensation (SFC) combines shallow and patch-embedded features through gated residual fusion before the backbone. The Collaborative Global–Local (CGL) module applies an additional refinement operation with shared parameters before token selection at two backbone stages. Pixel Contrastive Loss (PCL) uses center-pixel labels to supervise projected patch embeddings during training. The proposed method achieves overall accuracies of 96.50%, 97.60%, 95.35%, and 94.83% on the Pavia University, Houston13, Indian Pines, and WHU-HH datasets, respectively. Component comparisons and approximately parameter-matched controls characterize configuration-dependent effects. Numerical checks assess consistency between the stated operations and their implementation, and an additional Botswana experiment extends the evaluation to a satellite wetland and woodland scene.

title: Explainable Transformer-Based Estimation of Surface NO2 Concentrations Across Fujian Province Using TROPOMI Observations
summary: Atmospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is one of the major pollutants affecting environmental quality and human health, yet accurate surface NO2 (NO2Surface) estimation remains challenging due to complex nonlinear relationships between satellite-derived NO2 column density (NO2column) and near-surface concentrations. Here, we proposed an explainable transformer-based framework for daily NO2Surface estimation across Fujian Province, integrating Sentinel-5P TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) NO2 observations with meteorological data, digital elevation model (DEM), normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), nighttime light (NTL), and population density (PD). Using ground-based observations, Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) was trained and benchmarked against five conventional machine learning (ML) algorithms. Under random five-fold cross-validation, TabPFN achieved the highest accuracy, yielding a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.93, root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.56 μg m−3, mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.05 μg m−3, and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 5.82%, with R2 improvements of 0.17–0.26 and RMSE reductions of 45.3–53.5% relative to CatBoost and RF, respectively. Additional station-grouped spatial validation and independent temporal validation yielded R2 values of 0.86 and 0.79, respectively. The reconstructed NO2Surface distributions revealed a clear coastal-to-inland gradient, with concentrations frequently exceeding 50 μg m−3 in urbanized coastal areas but generally below 15 μg m−3 in northwestern mountainous regions. Strong seasonality was evident, with the peak NO2Surface and widespread pollution in winter, contrasting with lower and more localized levels in summer. Temporal analyses revealed persistent declines in NO2Surface, with annual mean concentrations decreasing by 11.7% from 2019 to 2020 and a further decline of 1.6% in 2021, while descriptive daily slopes were approximately −0.003 μg m−3 day−1. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlighted TROPOMI NO2column and BLH-corrected NO2 (NO2BLH) as the most influential predictors, accounting for 15.07% and 11.36% of the contribution, respectively, with temperature- and humidity-related variables exhibiting strong nonlinear responses. This study provides an accurate and interpretable framework for 1 km gridded NO2Surface estimation and characterizes the predictive relationships associated with regional NO2 variability.

title: Trajectory-SAM: Object Trajectory-Guided Segmentation for Remote Sensing Videos
summary: The rapid proliferation of high-resolution remote sensing video (RSV) has made object segmentation an increasingly critical yet challenging task. Existing methods face two fundamental limitations in this domain: (1) the intrinsic complexity of RSVs arising from diminutive object sizes, dense distributions, and drastic scale variations; (2) prohibitive computational overhead and latency caused by the massive spatial resolution of remote sensing imagery. To address these challenges, we propose Trajectory-SAM, a novel object trajectory-guided segmentation framework tailored for rapid and accurate object segmentation in RSVs. Specifically, we first employ a Graph Neural Network to extract representative keyframes, improving data utilization efficiency while suppressing attention drift and interpretation bias induced by redundant frames. We then introduce Temporal-LoRA, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy for the Segment Anything Model (SAM), substantially enhancing its spatiotemporal contextual understanding in remote sensing domains. Finally, we devise a sample-augmentation-based knowledge distillation strategy to accelerate inference without sacrificing segmentation quality. Extensive experiments on the SAT-MTB, iSAID, and VHR-10 datasets demonstrate that our proposed Trajectory-SAM achieves superior performance, establishing a compelling trade-off between accuracy and speed.

title: A Hierarchical Framework for Arctic Shoreline Type Mapping Using SAR and Optical Satellite Imagery
summary: Although intertidal-zone delineation and shoreline or coastal geomorphological classification have been extensively investigated, relatively few studies have integrated these complementary information layers within a unified and operational remote-sensing framework for oil-spill emergency response. With increasing development and marine transportation activities in the Arctic, detailed and spatially explicit shoreline information is essential for oil-spill response planning and coastal hazard assessment along the Canadian Arctic coast. A key challenge is to reliably characterize the spatial extent and geomorphological variability of Arctic intertidal shorelines under substantial temporal variability in tidal inundation and environmental conditions. This study presents a hierarchical shoreline classification framework designed to support oil-spill emergency preparedness and response planning. The framework integrates Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) backscatter, temporal-change and structural descriptors, and Sentinel-2 water-sensitive indices to derive a composite shore-zone proxy that captures spatial and temporal information on tidal inundation and coastal surface characteristics. This proxy supports Level 1 shore-zone mapping, while high-resolution optical imagery enables subsequent Level 2 shoreline-type classification. The framework was evaluated in four Canadian Arctic coastal areas representing diverse coastal landscapes and environmental conditions, including differences in tidal regimes, water turbidity, floating ice, and geomorphology. Results indicated that mapping accuracy remains constrained for tidal zones and substrates smaller than or comparable to the sensor’s spatial resolution. For Level 1 shore-zone mapping, unsupervised classification of the temporal and composite indices achieved overall mapping accuracies of 56–73% for the Upper Shore Zone across three study areas. For Level 2 shoreline-type mapping, Random Forest classification of high-resolution satellite imagery, including WorldView and GeoEye imagery, achieved overall accuracies of 81–85% across the four study areas. These results demonstrate the potential of the composite shore-zone proxy to integrate complementary SAR and optical information for consistent characterization of Arctic shore zones, while the subsequent shoreline-type classification provides additional geomorphological detail. Together, the hierarchical products provide spatially explicit shoreline information that can support the identification and prioritization of shoreline areas for oil-spill response planning and resource allocation.

title: Unraveling Spatial Associations of Surface Subsidence in Typical Oil Production Areas of Songyuan City by Integrating Time-Series InSAR and Deep Learning
summary: Oilfield subsidence threatens infrastructure and sustainable development. Although facility detection, factor-association analysis, and deformation forecasting have each advanced considerably, their systematic integration remains insufficiently explored for oilfields in agricultural plains, where C-band SAR decorrelation over cropland and wetland yields sparse and uneven deformation observations. This constraint complicates facility extraction, quantitative analysis of associations among interacting factors, and robust temporal prediction. To address these challenges, this study develops and applies an integrated modular workflow for the monitoring, analysis and prediction of surface subsidence in a typical oil production area of Songyuan City, China. We first used PS-InSAR for high-precision deformation monitoring and validated the results with leveling survey data. Subsequently, the YOLOv12 model was utilized for automated oil well identification, and the Geodetector model was applied to quantify the spatial associations between subsidence and the examined natural and anthropogenic factors. Finally, a hybrid LSTM–Transformer model was developed for time-series prediction and applied to forecast deformation through November 2025, twelve months beyond the final SAR acquisition. Results indicate significant spatial differentiation in deformation, with a maximum subsidence rate of −26.0 mm/y. Analysis identifies oil well density and surface elevation as the leading spatial factors among those examined, and the buffer zone analysis indicates a distance-related association of approximately 700 m between oil wells and subsidence rates. The hybrid model demonstrated superior overall accuracy compared to standalone LSTM and Transformer models. The findings provide concrete scientific support for risk mitigation in oil cities.

title: Optical Multispectral Indices Versus Microwave-Based Soil Water Index for Surface Soil Moisture Assessment: A Linear Mixed-Effects Analysis of Pixel-Level Heterogeneity over a Tuscan Agricultural Landscape
summary: Soil moisture (SM) assessment underpins applications ranging from climatological studies to land management and emergency response. Microwave techniques already support operational SM products, but at a spatial resolution limited to 1 km. Optical multispectral indices have been proposed as a complementary source of information at finer resolutions (10–100 m), yet vegetation heterogeneity has generally been handled by masking or stratifying the land cover rather than by modeling its effect. Here, we compare three indices (the Normalized Difference Infrared Index, NDII; the Normalized Multi-band Drought Index, NMDI; and the Visible and Shortwave Infrared Drought Index, VSDI) over a heterogeneous agricultural area near Grosseto, Tuscany, using 31 Landsat-8 OLI images acquired over four summers. Evaluated against the Copernicus Soil Water Index (SWI), VSDI performed best both when averaged over the test area and when analyzed at the pixel level (1 km) and was therefore selected for further analysis. A linear mixed-effects model with pixel-dependent intercepts resolves a within-pixel VSDI–SWI repeated measures correlation of 0.714, against 0.411 for the pooled regression. Allowing the slope to vary as well shows that vegetation density governs both the baseline level of VSDI and its sensitivity to soil moisture, with the within-pixel correlation falling from 0.84 on bare soil to 0.30 under a dense canopy.

title: A Transformer Network for Settlement Generalization Integrating Raster Maps and Remote Sensing Images
summary: To address the challenges of reliance on manual expertise and insufficient automation and intelligence in settlement generalization during scale transformation, this paper proposes a multi-scale settlement generalization model (DSG-Trans) based on the fusion of dual-source data: raster maps and remote sensing images. Leveraging the cartographic correspondence between remote sensing image resolution and map scale, this model integrates source-scale maps with specific low-resolution remote sensing imagery to automatically generate target-scale raster maps that adhere to cartographic specifications. The model employs a bidirectional cross-attention mechanism and a Transformer architecture to facilitate the semantic integration of dual-source data, while a progressive upsampling strategy is utilized to reconstruct spatial details. Additionally, a composite loss function incorporating four constraints is designed to enhance the quality of settlement generalization. Experiments were conducted in New York City, USA, using a multi-source dataset constructed from 3D-GloBFP building footprint data and multi-source remote sensing imagery, focusing on two scale transformation scenarios: 1:5000 to 1:10,000 and 1:5000 to 1:25,000. The results indicate that the proposed method effectively learns and simulates expert generalization knowledge, significantly improving the automation level and scale adaptability of map generalization while preserving geometric morphology and spatial distribution patterns.

title: 3DMAUNet: A 3D Memory-Augmented Deep Unfolding Network with Dynamic Momentum Updating for Snapshot Compressive Spectral Imaging
summary: Coded aperture snapshot spectral compressive imaging (CASSI) enables the recovery of hyperspectral images (HSIs) from a single two-dimensional compressive measurement, serving as a core paradigm in modern computational imaging. However, HSI reconstruction from under-sampled measurements is a severely ill-posed inverse problem. Existing deep unfolding methods typically treat each iterative stage independently and model spatial–spectral features in a decoupled manner, which neglects intrinsic spatial–spectral coupling and lacks persistent cross-stage information propagation. To tackle these issues, we propose a deep dynamic 3D memory-augmented unfolding network (3DMAUNet) for HSI reconstruction. Based on the momentum-accelerated generalized alternating projection framework, 3DMAUNet retains the strict mathematical interpretability of iterative optimization while integrating data-driven learnable components. Specifically, we design two key modules: (1) a 3D memory-augmented learning module equipped with a persistent memory bank, which explicitly encodes cross-layer spatial–spectral correlations to enable efficient inter-stage information transfer and long-range dependency modeling; and (2) a learnable dynamic fast momentum updating module, which fuses cross-stage spatial–spectral attention features to estimate task-adaptive momentum coefficients, accelerating convergence and enhancing the robustness of feature updating. Comprehensive experiments on synthetic and real-world HSI datasets demonstrate that 3DMAUNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative and qualitative reconstruction performance.

title: Estimating Downward Shortwave Radiation over Complex Terrain: Synergizing Sentinel-2 Imagery and Topographic Data via Physics-Guided XGBoost
summary: Downward shortwave radiation (DSR) varies strongly across mountain slopes, and products designed for horizontal surfaces may not resolve this variability. We estimated slope-parallel DSR at eight Saihanba sites using Sentinel-2 imagery, topography, atmospheric inputs, and BRDF-informed surface albedo. Both branches used XGBoost, with the clear-sky branch further incorporating a parameterized radiation anchor, bounded residual learning, and support-aware output correction. On the 2024 test set (n = 1451), the full framework achieved an RMSE of 92.60 W/m2, an NRMSE of 15.79% and an R2 of 0.897. Pooled leave-one-site-out validation across all 6096 samples yielded an RMSE of 113.68 W/m2. For horizontal-surface observations at 10 Heihe River Basin stations, NRMSE was 17.60%. Clear-sky estimates depended most on solar-incidence geometry, whereas top-of-atmosphere spectra dominated the cloudy-sky XGBoost model.

title: Cross-Field Transfer of UAV-Based Winter Wheat Yield Prediction: Model Transferability and Sample Efficiency
summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing is widely used for plot-scale crop yield prediction, but model performance may decline when models are transferred across fields with different crop, environmental, management, and sensing conditions. This study evaluated the cross-field transferability of UAV-based winter wheat yield models using multispectral (MS), RGB, and thermal infrared (TIR) information. Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models were evaluated under five strategies: target-only training (T1), direct transfer (T2), nitrogen-based adaptation (T3), cultivar-based adaptation (T4), and mixed adaptation (T5). Direct transfer increased the normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) from 12.7% to 14.0% for CatBoost and from 12.9% to 15.9% for MLP. Mixed adaptation achieved the best overall performance, with coefficient of determination (R2) values of 0.84 and 0.87 and NRMSE values of 11.7% and 10.9% for CatBoost and MLP, respectively. After controlling for calibration sample size, the difference between T3 and T4 became smaller, indicating that adaptation performance was influenced by both calibration-data composition and sample availability. CatBoost showed diminishing returns near the 40% calibration level in this experiment, whereas MLP continued to benefit from additional target-domain samples. Prediction errors were higher for samples beyond the source-domain yield range, while mixed adaptation reduced prediction errors in both yield-range groups. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and sensor-level ablation showed that MS features provided important predictive information, while RGB and TIR provided complementary information. These results indicate that target-domain adaptation can improve cross-field UAV yield prediction and highlight the importance of calibration design, yield-range mismatch, and multi-sensor information when transferring models to new fields.

title: Effect of Sun Glints from Ice Clouds on MODIS Data Products
summary: This paper examines the way sun glints from horizontally oriented ice crystals that occur in clouds impact atmospheric data products provided by the Moderate-Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS). For this, the paper presents a statistical analysis of two years of MODIS data from all tropical land regions. The results indicate only weak glint effects on cloud amount and height, as these values are obtained using mainly observations of (inherently glint-free) thermal infrared radiation. In contrast, glints are found to cause a roughly 10% increase in mean retrieved cloud optical thickness, and 10% decreases in mean particle size and in the prevalence of ice cloud phase. Moreover, glints from undetected ice clouds are found to cause roughly 5% increases in mean aerosol optical depth and coarse mode fraction, and positive and negative biases comparable to the magnitude of the seasonal cycle in total column ozone and precipitable water vapor amounts, respectively. Given the modest size of glints, the effects are most important to consider in studies that use data from a limited range of viewing zenith angles (e.g., around nadir). The results are relevant to MODIS and to other satellite imagers that use similar retrieval algorithms, and thus likely experience similar glint effects.

title: High-Resolution Burned Area Mapping Using Sentinel-2 Imagery and Robust Satellite Techniques
summary: High accuracy in burned area (BA) mapping is desirable for many fire-related applications. Most operational products are based on coarse-resolution satellite data with a final spatial resolution ranging from 250 m to 1000 m. The use of higher-resolution satellite data, such as that from the Multispectral Imager (MSI) on board Sentinel-2, is usually reserved for generating BA products only for specific countries and time periods. Moreover, BA algorithms are typically driven by fire detection products to minimize false identifications. The resulting accuracy of such BA products depends strongly on land cover, fire regime, and the reliability of the considered fire detection products. In this paper, we exploit the multitemporal Robust Satellite Technique (RST) to identify burned areas and implement a workflow based on Sentinel-2 images within Google Earth Engine. Test results from two complete region-wide experiments conducted under contrasting seasonal, phenological, and agricultural conditions showed that 97.85% of the mapped area was confirmed as burned within the adopted multi-source validation framework, with an area-based commission error of 1.38% and omission error of 0.60%. Missed detections documented by the Regional Spatial Data Infrastructure (RSDI) amounted to 10.60 ha, corresponding to approximately 0.9% of the burned area reported by RSDI over the tested periods. Polygon-level intercomparison with RSDI and the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) yielded Intersection over Union (IoU) values of 0.69 and 0.83, respectively. The proposed approach mapped larger burned areas than those reported by both RSDI (+48%) and EFFIS (+143%) as well.

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Nonparametric SAR Autofocus Using a Hybrid Architecture
summary: Autofocus plays a pivotal role in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging, which is particularly crucial for high-resolution applications. Traditional autofocus methods face inherent limitations, such as reliance on strong isolated scatterers within the scene or prohibitive computational complexity, making them inadequate for the practical demands of the rapid and batch processing of massive SAR imagery. Although recent deep learning (DL)-based methods have improved focusing efficiency, they predominantly rely on predefined high-order polynomial models for phase error estimation, which inevitably introduces parameter redundancy, restricts the model’s adaptability to complex phase errors, and is highly prone to inducing severe oscillations at the aperture boundaries. To overcome these limitations, this article proposes DeepAutofocus, a non-parametric deep learning framework for SAR autofocus. First, we design a physics-inspired subaperture correlation Transformer architecture. A multiscale convolutional neural network (CNN) is utilized to extract local spatial features, which are then transformed into serialized subaperture image patches. Subsequently, the self-attention mechanism of the Transformer is employed to capture the long-range dependencies across subapertures. Second, we introduce a data-driven cubic B-spline reconstruction strategy that directly estimates phase errors without depending on predefined high-order polynomial models, thereby eliminating boundary oscillations while maintaining high flexibility. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real measured satellite datasets demonstrate that, compared to traditional autofocus algorithms and existing DL-based methods, the proposed DeepAutofocus achieves superior focusing performance under various complex phase error conditions.

title: Soil Moisture Retrieval from Sentinel-1 SAR in Arid Oasis Regions: Error Analysis and Incidence Angle Effects
summary: High-precision inversion of soil moisture content using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data still faces significant technical challenges, as the radar backscatter coefficient is influenced by complex interactions among surface roughness, vegetation cover, and soil permittivity. Therefore, systematically evaluating the mechanisms by which SAR system parameters and surface environmental variables influence soil moisture inversion is of critical scientific importance. This study utilized an improved alpha approximation algorithm in conjunction with Sentinel-1 SAR data to estimate soil moisture content for different land cover types in middle reaches of the Heihe River Basin and analyzed the sources of error in the soil moisture estimation process. The results indicate that the improved alpha approximation algorithm can achieve relatively satisfactory soil moisture inversion results. However, significant differences in the inversion results were still observed under different orbital and incidence angle conditions, with an average RMSE of 0.034 for ascending orbits and 0.037 for descending orbits. In desert regions, data from Ascending Orbit 128 with an incidence angle of 33° yielded the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE, 0.030 m3/m3) and the highest determination coefficient (R2, 0.848). In agricultural areas, the minimum RMSE for 2017 and 2018 was 0.030 m3/m3 and 0.041 m3/m3, respectively, while the maximum R2 values were 0.815 and 0.728, respectively; Compared with the desert region, the accuracy of soil moisture inversion in the agricultural region was reduced due to the influence of vegetation phenology and irrigation activities. Overall, the soil moisture inversion results for both study areas agreed well with field observations but still exhibited significant seasonal and interannual variations. The angle of incidence, surface roughness, vegetation dynamics, precipitation conditions, and irrigation activities were the primary factors affecting the accuracy of soil moisture inversion. Especially, the impact of the static roughness assumption on the accuracy of the alpha approximation algorithm is more pronounced.

title: PRIVER: Prompt-Stable Reciprocal Inter-Scale Visual Evidence Reranking for High-Resolution Remote-Sensing Imagery
summary: High-resolution remote-sensing images contain dense object layouts and fine spatial details, but their spatial extent makes direct vision–language interpretation difficult. Patch retrieval offers a practical alternative by returning local regions as candidate evidence for downstream interpretation. However, independent semantic scores can leave relevant patches at isolated ranks or return lists with substantial irrelevant content. We propose Prompt-Stable Reciprocal Inter-scale Visual Evidence Reranking (PRIVER), a post-retrieval method for ranking patches within one image using controlled object-category queries. It aggregates four predefined prompt templates and combines semantic scores with geometric support, principally from a degree-normalized inter-scale graph. No encoder weights are updated, and retrieval and reranking do not access object annotations. Parameters are selected on annotated DOTA-v1.5 development data and held fixed. With relevance defined by annotated object coverage, Precision@10 on 458 DOTA-v1.5 internal-test images increases from 0.567 to 0.625 (absolute gain 0.058; 95% source-image cluster bootstrap interval [0.052, 0.065]). Normalized discounted cumulative gain at rank 10 (nDCG@10) increases from 0.647 to 0.730 and distinct-object coverage at rank 10 from 0.773 to 0.873. On a disjoint 526-image SODA-A subset, the corresponding metrics increase from 0.414 to 0.502, 0.445 to 0.550, and 0.467 to 0.681. Coverage-based gains persist with GeoRSCLIP and RemoteCLIP and under altered tiling policies on fixed image subsets. Inter-scale support is the principal source of improvement. These results support training-free, coverage-defined patch prioritization for within-image visual evidence retrieval.

title: LuTan-1 InSAR-Constrained Reconstruction of Concealed Coal-Mining Working-Face Geometry
summary: To address the difficulty in determining underground working face geometry when mining records are incomplete or mining activities are concealed, this study proposes an InSAR-constrained method for inverting the geometric parameters of concealed working faces. The method uses the line-of-sight (LOS) deformation field derived from LuTan-1 InSAR observations as the primary input. The search ranges of mining depth, mining thickness, coal seam dip angle, strike azimuth, working face center coordinates, strike length, and dip length are constrained using the morphology of the subsidence basin, available empirical parameters, and the Probability Integral Method (PIM). These constraints reduce the uncertainty caused by a large search space and parameter coupling in high-dimensional inversion. An adaptive multi-strategy differential evolution algorithm is then introduced. Latin hypercube sampling is used for population initialization. Dynamic parameter adjustment, multiple mutation strategies, reflective boundary handling, and local refinement are incorporated to improve optimization stability in complex parameter spaces. The simulation results show that the proposed method generally outperforms particle swarm optimization, genetic algorithm, evolutionary strategy, and standard differential evolution in inversion accuracy, convergence stability, and robustness to errors. It can reliably recover the main geometric parameters of a predefined working face. In the engineering case study of the 97,315 working face, the inverted active-mining geometry during the LuTan-1 observation period is generally consistent with the corresponding mine records, with a deformation-fitting RMSE of 32.53 mm and relative errors of the main geometric parameters below 7.9%. Parameter sensitivity analysis further shows that the geometric dimensions and center location of the working face have pronounced effects on the LOS deformation field. These parameters should therefore be tightly constrained during inversion. The results demonstrate that the proposed method provides a feasible remote-sensing approach for identifying concealed working faces and estimating goaf geometric parameters in mining areas with incomplete records.

title: LiDAR-Assisted Survey Locates Unregistered Rock Shelters in the Blue Mountains, Australia
summary: Rock shelters are important cultural and archaeological sites in Australia, often containing evidence of Aboriginal occupation and symbolic expression. While rock shelters have been investigated across Australia, locating them in rugged environments through pedestrian surveys remains challenging. This research contributes a methodology which integrates remote sensing, GIS analyses, and archaeological survey to locate rock shelters in the Blue Mountains. We produced models in ArcGIS Pro that analyse high-resolution, UAV-based LiDAR datasets and publicly available, low-resolution, aircraft-based LiDAR datasets from the New South Wales government. Our models yield locations of potential rock shelters, which can be visually evaluated in 3D LiDAR point clouds and ground-truthed through archaeological survey. Ground-truthing confirmed the successful detection of six known rock shelters on UAV and NSW LiDAR datasets, producing more accurate coordinates than the ones listed in online databases. Significantly, we identified three previously unregistered rock shelters that preserve rock art and lithics. These promising results indicate capacity to improve the spatial accuracy of legacy site records and locate unregistered archaeological rock shelters within, and potentially beyond, Australia. Our methodology promotes targeted and efficient survey of rock shelters that can produce regional datasets benefitting local communities, archaeology, and cultural heritage management.

title: Water Quality Variation Among Optical Water Types Along the Guangdong Coast: Additional Within-Class Information from Membership Structure
summary: Coastal waters exhibit pronounced spatial and temporal variability in optical properties and water quality, which cannot be fully characterized by observations from discrete monitoring stations. Satellite Optical Water Type (OWT) classification provides spatially continuous information on optical conditions. However, comparisons with water quality observations have generally relied on the assigned OWT, and it remains unclear whether membership provides additional information within the same class. This study examined the relationships of assigned OWTs and membership with monthly water quality conditions in Guangdong coastal waters. Sentinel-3 OLCI observations acquired from 2017 to 2024 were matched with station observations of dissolved inorganic nitrogen (DIN), dissolved inorganic phosphorus (DIP), chemical oxygen demand (COD), dissolved oxygen (DO), and eutrophication classes. The analysis first compared water quality among assigned OWTs and then evaluated the secondary OWT and membership values within OWT 4a, the class with the largest sample size. Assigned OWTs distinguished broad differences in DIN, DIP, COD, and eutrophication classes, whereas DO did not differ significantly among OWTs. Within OWT 4a, the class associated with the second highest membership separated records with different nutrient, COD, and eutrophication conditions. Continuous membership values provided further information, but their relationships with water quality depended on the secondary OWT and were most consistent for DIN. OWT occurrence and station eutrophication patterns showed partial spatial correspondence, particularly around the Pearl River Estuary and Huangmao Bay. These findings show that assigned OWTs identify broad water quality differences, while secondary OWTs and membership values distinguish additional variation within OWT 4a. The mapped optical patterns provide complementary spatial context for interpreting station-based water quality observations.

title: Automatic Extraction of Discontinuity Traces from Rock Mass Point Cloud Data Using PhaseVote
summary: Accurate and thorough detection of rock mass discontinuities is essential in geotechnical engineering as they have a significant impact on the stability of underground and surface excavations, yet they are difficult to automate. In the work reported here, an automatic algorithm, termed PhaseVote, is proposed for the extraction of discontinuity traces from the colour (RGB) attributes of 3D meshes which, combined with the region growing method, can help derive more accurate discontinuity modelling of a rock mass. Conventional edge detection methods degrade under low contrast and variable illumination, and geometry-based point-cloud methods overlook spectral features. The proposed approach uses contrast-invariant phase-based feature detection. The detected edges are filtered and then extended or pruned to form major discontinuity traces using the tensor voting method. The first algorithm, phase analysis, detects edges independently of local contrast, while the latter, tensor voting, links and denoises the resultant edge fragments into continuous traces using perceptual grouping. The detection capability of the proposed method is assessed by applying it to two case studies and comparing the results with an existing method. PhaseVote achieved detection rates of 94.85% and 84.72% and IoUs of 70.27% and 69.80%, compared with 76.12%/45.95% and 69.81%/43.81% for a conventional existing method. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is resilient to image contrast, robust to changes in the orientation of discontinuity planes, is less subjective and has a higher degree of automation.

title: APFNet: An Adaptive Perception Fusion Network for Multi-Scale Object Detection in Remote Sensing
summary: Accurate multi-scale object detection remains challenging in remote sensing (RS) imagery due to severe scale variation, limited pixel occupancy of small targets, and complex backgrounds. Existing multi-scale fusion methods propagate features along predefined cross-scale paths and apply receptive fields fixed once trained, so fusion weights and the spatial range of contextual evidence remain largely input-independent. The Adaptive Perception Fusion Network (APFNet) targets these two aspects through four operations: (1) Split-ELAN (SP-ELAN), a channel-compressed serial refinement backbone whose design is motivated by small-object feature preservation; (2) Adaptive Sampling (AS), which produces sample-dependent channel weights from a global descriptor during cross-scale alignment; (3) Adaptive Gating (AG), which is coupled with AS and aggregates the recalibrated features at complementary receptive-field scales; and (4) Adaptive Context Aggregation (ACA), which aligns three feature levels and applies parallel large-kernel depthwise branches to supply broader multi-scale context. On DIOR, APFNet-L achieves three-run mean values of 86.39% AP50, 63.09% AP, and 26.10% APS. A complete 23 component-group study under one scratch/no-augmentation protocol yields positive conditional contrasts for SP-ELAN, ACA, and the coupled AS–AG pathway. LEVIR and RSOD provide additional cross-dataset and configuration-selection results. These operations use established primitives; the contribution lies in their routing and aggregation.

title: Seasonal Prior-Guided Dynamic Forecasting of Nonstationary Gridded PM2.5 Concentrations in China
summary: Accurate and timely short-term forecasting of gridded PM2.5 concentrations is essential for air-quality management and public health protection, especially for the growing elderly population who are particularly vulnerable to air pollution. Advances in multi-source environmental data and deep learning have substantially improved the spatiotemporal prediction of PM2.5 concentrations. However, existing studies have mainly focused on developing increasingly sophisticated model architectures and optimization strategies while insufficiently considering the temporal nonstationarity of PM2.5 pollution and the recurrent characteristics associated with similar seasonal environmental regimes. Changes in natural environmental conditions and anthropogenic emissions can continuously alter the relationships governing PM2.5 concentrations, challenging the stability of continuous short-term forecasting; meanwhile, historically recurring seasonal pollution characteristics provide potentially valuable prior information for model adaptation. To address this problem, we propose a Seasonal Prior-guided Elastic Weight Consolidation (Seasonal EWC) framework for dynamic forecasting of nonstationary gridded PM2.5 concentrations in China. The framework derives season-specific parameter anchors and Fisher-based parameter importance from historical seasonal conditions and uses this prior knowledge to guide parameter updates during continuous short-term forecasting. Experiments with four representative spatiotemporal forecasting models showed that Seasonal EWC produced architecture-dependent changes in forecasting performance, reducing the annual mean MAE and RMSE by 30.3% and 31.7% for U-Net and by 10.9% and 7.6% for Earthformer, with only small improvements for IAM4VP and mixed changes for ConvLSTM. Parameter analysis revealed that Seasonal EWC reduced parameter-update magnitudes by approximately 27–32% and substantially limited long-term parameter deviation, indicating more stable adaptation during continuous forecasting. These findings demonstrate that seasonal prior knowledge can effectively guide dynamic model adaptation under evolving PM2.5 conditions, providing a promising approach for continuous short-term air-quality forecasting.

title: Echo-Driven Doppler Parameter Estimation for High-Resolution Squinted Spaceborne Sliding Spotlight SAR
summary: High-resolution squinted spaceborne sliding spotlight synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging requires accurate Doppler parameters. In conventional SAR processing, Doppler parameters are generally derived from prior ancillary information or estimated from the received echoes. However, Doppler parameters derived from prior information are sensitive to ancillary-measurement errors, while existing echo-based methods remain insufficient for ambiguity-resolved Doppler-centroid estimation and Doppler frequency modulation (FM)-rate refinement in high-resolution squinted sliding spotlight SAR. To reduce the reliance on prior ancillary information for Doppler-parameter determination, this paper proposes an echo-driven Doppler-parameter estimation (ED-DPE) method. The proposed method first estimates the baseband Doppler centroid using adjacent-echo cross-correlation and then resolves the Doppler ambiguity number based on the range-migration slope, thereby obtaining the absolute Doppler centroid fd. The estimated absolute Doppler centroid is subsequently used as a physical constraint on an attitude-equivalent observation geometry, which is refined through contrast-based full-aperture image formation to obtain the Doppler FM rate fr and the imaging parameters. Point-target simulations and real spaceborne SAR experiments demonstrate that the proposed ED-DPE method supports accurate focusing of 0.25-m-resolution squinted sliding spotlight SAR.

title: Susceptibility Zoning of Seasonal Freeze–Thaw Deformation in Permafrost Subgrade Along the Qinghai–Tibet Highway
summary: Permafrost subgrades along the Qinghai–Tibet Highway exhibit pronounced spatial variability in seasonal freeze–thaw deformation under the combined effects of complex permafrost conditions, climate change, and engineering disturbances. Focusing on the Xidatan–Tuojula Mountains section, this study integrated field monitoring, borehole investigations, subgrade geometric parameters, and multisource remote sensing data to establish a coupled ground–atmosphere model. The maximum refreezing depth (Hf) was selected as the susceptibility indicator, and an extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model based on 172 numerical simulations was developed to predict the spatial distribution of seasonal freeze–thaw deformation susceptibility at a 30 m resolution. The predicted susceptibility index was classified into five levels using the Jenks natural breaks method. The results show that susceptibility along the 532.20 km investigated section exhibits significant spatial heterogeneity. Level I sections account for the largest proportion (30.64%), followed by Level II (18.52%), Level IV (15.40%), Level V (9.54%), and Level III (7.92%). High-susceptibility sections are mainly concentrated in Hoh Xil, Wudaoliang, the Fenghuo Mountains, and the Tanggula Mountains, whereas low-susceptibility sections are primarily distributed in the Tuotuo River Basin, Tongtian River Basin, Wenquan Basin, and the Tuojula Mountains section. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified mean annual ground temperature (MAGT), subgrade height (SH), and ice content type (ICT) as the dominant controlling factors, contributing 51.59%, 26.56%, and 18.16%, respectively. The interactions between MAGT × SH and MAGT × ICT were identified as the dominant two-way interactions. These findings provide insights for identifying critical sections, optimizing monitoring strategies, and supporting zonation-based maintenance of permafrost highways.

title: A Few-Shot Method Based on Spatial-Frequency Dual-Domain Feature Enhancement and Hypersphere Mapping Constraint for SAR Ship Recognition
summary: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can acquire maritime imagery independently of daylight and under diverse weather conditions, which makes it well suited to persistent ship monitoring and maritime awareness. Nevertheless, recognizing SAR ships from only a few labeled examples remains difficult for several reasons. First, sea clutter and speckle noise may weaken ship-related structural and scattering-response information. Second, features from different categories may become difficult to separate because between-class differences are small while within-class variations remain substantial. Third, when each category contains only a few support examples, an abnormal or noisy sample can noticeably distort the estimated prototype. To address these issues, a few-shot SAR ship recognition method based on spatial-frequency dual-domain feature enhancement and hypersphere mapping constraint (SFHMC) is proposed. First, the spatial-frequency feature enhancement and extraction module (SFEE) combines the Haar discrete wavelet transform with multi-scale spatial modeling. It enhances structural, textural, and scattering-response features under complex backgrounds. Second, the hypersphere mapping constraint module (HMCM) normalizes support and query embeddings onto a unit hypersphere. By removing differences in feature magnitude, this mapping makes similarity estimation depend mainly on feature direction and produces a more structured class distribution. Third, the sample-weighted prototype generation module (SWPGM) adaptively adjusts the contribution of each support sample according to its consistency with the initial class prototype. This reduces prototype bias caused by noisy or atypical samples. The three modules jointly optimize feature representation, metric discrimination, and prototype calibration. Experiments are conducted on FUSAR-Ship and OpenSARShip, with additional validation on MSTAR under 3-way 1-shot and 3-way 5-shot settings. Compared with MBEN-BC, SFHMC improves classification accuracy by 1.41 and 1.96 percentage points on FUSAR-Ship, 2.68 and 4.46 percentage points on OpenSARShip, and 6.40 and 0.48 percentage points on MSTAR, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SFHMC for few-shot SAR target recognition under limited data and complex imaging conditions.

title: LD-DETR: A Multi-Scale Landslide Detection and Segmentation Network for Complex Geological Environments
summary: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards. High-resolution remote sensing imagery provides an effective means for landslide detection and mapping, supporting geological hazard assessment and early warning. However, existing methods still face challenges in complex mountainous scenes with heterogeneous land cover and geological conditions. These challenges include irregular segmentation boundaries caused by diverse landslide shapes, small-scale detection difficulties due to background interference, and foreground–background class imbalance that hinders effective model optimization. To address these issues, we propose LD-DETR, a network for landslide detection and segmentation. An Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module is integrated into the segmentation head to improve multi-scale feature representation, enabling better segmentation of landslides with varying spatial sizes. To alleviate class imbalance caused by the dominance of non-landslide pixels, a weighted Tversky Loss is introduced to improve the learning of hard samples. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is further combined with orientation-aware data augmentation to enable parameter-efficient adaptation, reducing the proportion of trainable parameters of LD-DETR to 41.07% while keeping the pre-trained backbone parameters frozen. Experiments on the Bijie and Luding Landslide Dataset (BLLD) demonstrate that LD-DETR is competitive with the baseline model and several YOLO-based approaches. The proposed method achieves an F1-score of 95.18% and a Recall of 95%, while the segmentation task reaches an mAP of 59.28%, slightly higher than the RF-DETR baseline. Furthermore, a limited-sample adaptation experiment on the Jiuzhai landslide dataset demonstrates the transferability of the proposed method across different geographic regions. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides competitive landslide detection and segmentation performance and offers an approach for fine-grained landslide mapping using remote sensing imagery.

title: DCA-Net: Deep Context Aggregation Network for Remote Sensing Object Detection
summary: Object detection in remote sensing scenarios faces multiple challenges, primarily manifested in multi-scale objects, class imbalance, densely packed small targets, and occlusion. To address these issues, we propose DCA-Net, an object detection method based on deep context aggregation. Built upon the YOLO architecture, the proposed method introduces parallel multi-branch pooling paths and an adaptive feature reweighting mechanism to construct a deep context aggregation backbone (DCA-Backbone). This enables efficient fusion and selective enhancement of multi-scale contextual semantic information. Furthermore, a detection head based on efficient channel interaction (ECI-Head) is designed to enhance the representational capability for multi-scale objects and complex morphological features. Experimental results demonstrate that DCA-Net achieves mAP50:95 of 50.5% on DIOR dataset and 61.5% on NWPU VHR-10 dataset, achieving competitive performance compared with other methods. Extensive visualization and ablation experiments further validate its detection accuracy and robustness in complex remote sensing scenarios.

title: Shape-Adaptive Learning and Style-Aware Decomposition for Domain-Generalized Oriented Object Detection
summary: Oriented object detection is essential for interpreting high-resolution remote-sensing images, but detectors trained on a single source domain often suffer from severe performance degradation under unseen imaging conditions. Existing domain generalization methods mainly address horizontal detection or treat style variation as an undifferentiated perturbation, while the geometry-sensitive nature of oriented objects, especially elongated instances, is insufficiently considered. To address these limitations, a shape-adaptive learning and style-aware decomposition framework, termed SA-DGOD, is proposed for single-source domain-generalized oriented object detection. A frozen CLIP image encoder is employed only during training to provide multi-level style statistics, from which several interpretable branch-style pseudo-domains are constructed by modulating feature statistics that characterize photometric and contrast variations. These explicit pseudo-domain identities enable structured style diversification without accessing target-domain data. To improve orientation-sensitive representation learning, a shape-adaptive soft consistency loss is introduced for rotated RoI features.
