Instead of using a fixed-threshold binary weighting scheme, the proposed loss adopts an aspect-ratio-aware threshold and a continuous rotated-IoU-based weight, allowing elongated objects and geometrically reliable proposals to be handled more flexibly. Furthermore, a style-aware common-specific classifier decomposition is introduced into the proposed framework to separate domain-invariant category discrimination from pseudo-domain-specific style bias. Extensive experiments on multiple remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization capability of SA-DGOD.

title: Adaptive Timing of Landslide Susceptibility Map Updates Using Persistent Deformation Changes
summary: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) provides spatially extensive deformation measurements that support dynamic landslide susceptibility assessment. However, determining when landslide susceptibility maps require updating remains insufficiently studied. Here, we introduce the persistent deformation-change area ratio (PDAR), the percentage of monitored slope-unit area exhibiting persistent velocity changes relative to each unit’s accepted reference. Three-observation confirmation and reference resetting allow update intervals to respond to both increasing and decreasing deformation. A common asymmetric matrix combines the current susceptibility class with the relative velocity change, allowing at most two upward steps or one downward step. We compared PDAR with no updating and fixed one-, three-, six- and twelve-month schedules across 6956 slope units in Yunyang, Kaizhou and Wushan. Baseline construction used 2013–2016, parameter calibration used 2017–2018, and evaluation covered 2019–2022. PDAR achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC; 0.7913 versus 0.6848 without updating), highest high/very high event capture (63.99%) and lowest false-positive rate (FPR; 13.67%). Relative to monthly updating, AUC increased by 0.1162 and FPR decreased by 12.92 percentage points. PDAR also exceeded the strongest fixed schedule, six-month updating, by 0.0688 in AUC. The fixed-window comparison showed that more frequent updating was not always beneficial. PDAR provides a state-dependent basis for selecting update windows rather than updating whenever newer observations become available.

title: Multi-Index Remote Sensing Assessment of Agro-Climatic Change and Agricultural Responses in Temperate and Semi-Arid Regions
summary: Diverse climatic regions exhibit unique agro-climatic vulnerabilities that are significantly shaped by climate stress. Understanding these distinct vulnerabilities is essential for developing effective policies to mitigate climate change impacts and ensuring sustainable environmental management. This study examines agro-climatic vulnerabilities in Nottinghamshire County (United Kingdom) and Udaipur District (India) from 2000 to 2024, comparing climate change impacts across temperate and semi-arid agricultural systems that represent fundamentally different system behaviours under contrasting climatic conditions. Using multi-temporal Landsat imagery and WorldClim climate data, nine environmental indices were analysed: the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), Moisture Stress Index (MSI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), Temperature Condition Index (TCI), Vegetation Health Index (VHI), Drought Risk Index (DRI), and Crop Health Index (CHI). The results reveal contrasting regional trajectories that challenge conventional assumptions about climate vulnerability. Udaipur exhibited improved vegetation and moisture conditions across the observation period, whereas Nottinghamshire showed intensifying moisture stress and declining precipitation. Warming was more pronounced in Nottinghamshire, while strong inter-index correlations validated the monitoring approach. These findings indicate that Udaipur benefits from intensified monsoon patterns, requiring flood mitigation and water-storage infrastructure, whereas Nottinghamshire’s rising moisture stress underscores the need for sustained monitoring and adaptive management. This comparative framework provides evidence-based insights for region-specific adaptation strategies essential to sustainable agricultural development across diverse agro-climatic zones.

title: Continuous Radar QPE Bias Field Reconstruction Through the Implicit Neural Representation Framework: QPE-BiasINR
summary: Biases in high-spatiotemporal-resolution radar quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) can substantially compromise the reliability of meteorological and hydrological disaster warning. Existing QPE correction methods commonly assume predefined spatial smoothness, whereas localized biases can vary sharply over short spatial distances. We therefore propose an implicit neural representation (INR) framework for continuous radar QPE bias-field reconstruction (QPE-BiasINR). QPE-BiasINR introduces QPE-background modulation, which conditions bias estimation on the local precipitation context to account for precipitation-dependent spatial variations in radar QPE errors. Moreover, a multiscale spatial consistency (MSC) constraint is incorporated into the loss function to explicitly strengthen spatial consistency. QPE-BiasINR was evaluated using hourly multi-radar mosaic QPE and gauge observations within the coverage of four radars in the Daqing River Basin,China, during June–September 2023. Test set performance was benchmarked against the uncorrected radar QPE, mean-field bias correction, and Kriging. QPE-BiasINR achieved the highest correlation coefficient (0.84) and the lowest root mean square error (3.29 mm) and mean absolute error (1.68 mm). Ablation experiments on QPE-BiasINR demonstrated that QPE-background modulation improved accuracy, while the MSC constraint reduced localized overcorrection. These results indicate that QPE-BiasINR can improve high-resolution radar QPE, with potential value for hydrological modeling and operational flood-risk monitoring.

title: Multisensor Analysis of Mediterranean Convective Case Studies Using EarthCARE and Meteosat Rapid Scan Observations
summary: Convection plays a key role in the Earth’s energy balance and is responsible for severe weather phenomena such as hailstorms, which cause significant damage to infrastructure and agriculture. This study investigates convective events over the Mediterranean Basin between September 2024 and September 2025 using a synergistic combination of active and passive satellite observations from geostationary (GEO) and low Earth orbit (LEO) platforms. Convective evolution is analyzed using EUMETSAT Satellite Application Facility on Support to Nowcasting and Very Short Range Forecasting products derived from Meteosat Rapid Scan Service imagery and the Multi-sensor Approach for Satellite Hail Advection (MASHA), which combines passive microwave hail probability retrievals from the Global Precipitation Measurement constellation with high-temporal-resolution Meteosat infrared observations to monitor hail-producing storms in near real time. The analysis is further enhanced with EarthCARE Cloud Profiling Radar reflectivity and Doppler velocity measurements, whose spatial variability provides a proxy for identifying convective cores and storm intensity. For selected events, observations from the Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager are also examined, highlighting the close relationship between intense lightning activity and strong convective updrafts. The results demonstrate the potential of combining complementary satellite observations to improve the detection and characterization of severe convection and hail-producing storms and identify the key roadblocks and pathways towards the effective integration of LEO and GEO observations.

title: Joint Super-Resolution and Weighted Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition for Ground Penetrating Radar Clutter Suppression
summary: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is an important non-destructive sensing technology for subsurface detection. However, strong clutter from surface reflection and heterogeneous media often masks weak target responses in B-scan images. Existing low-rank and sparse decomposition (LRSD) methods, such as Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA), can separate clutter and targets but suffer from uniform singular value shrinkage and high computational cost; more critically, they operate only at the original resolution, refining only the spatial sampling grid of the migrated image under the inherent physical resolution limit. In this paper, we propose a Joint Super-Resolution and Weighted Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition (JSR-LRSD) framework that synergistically suppresses clutter and improves the spatial detail and target localization of the migrated image without extending its physical resolution. Unlike cascade approaches, which perform clutter removal first and super-resolution afterward and may amplify residual clutter, our method integrates a differentiable super-resolution network directly into the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) iterations. This allows for the sparse target matrix to be regularized by high-resolution image priors, while the high-resolution estimate adaptively adjusts the weighted nuclear norm via total variation feedback. An adaptive weighted nuclear norm is designed using singular values of the observed data and the total variation feedback from the high-resolution target estimate. A randomized singular value decomposition (SVD) is introduced to accelerate computation. Extensive experiments on simulated and laboratory GPR data demonstrate that the proposed JSR-LRSD achieves a higher signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) compared to conventional and LRSD-based methods, with clear improvement in spatial detail recovery, while maintaining computational efficiency.

title: Reference Data Generation for Remote Sensing Image Classification: A Comprehensive Review of Methods, Challenges, and Recent Advances
summary: Image classification is a fundamental technique that has been broadly adopted in remote sensing, computer vision and related areas. High-quality annotated datasets are necessary for the development and reliable evaluation of classification and segmentation algorithms for accurate thematic mapping. Reference data are critical in this sense, as their quality has a direct impact on the performance, accuracy and generalization of the model. However, generating reliable reference data remains challenging due to methodological, technical, and annotation-related uncertainties. This study reviews the principal challenges in reference data generation, and the solutions proposed in scientific literature. A total of 100 papers indexed in the Web of Science were examined. The review covers traditional reference data generation methods as well as emerging approaches based on semi-supervised, self-supervised, and active learning, segmentation- and post-processing-assisted labeling, benchmark dataset construction, sampling and accuracy assessment, and deep learning and automated label generation. Major challenges and emerging research directions are also discussed. The results indicate a clear shift from traditional manual techniques to more automated, learning based and accuracy driven methods. The study provides a framework of existing techniques and future research areas in image classification.

title: Geodetic Deformation Inversion of Groundwater Variations in the Golmud River Basin, Northwestern China
summary: The Golmud River Basin is a typical inland arid river basin in the Qaidam Basin, and the dynamics of its groundwater storage are of great importance for regional ecological security and water resources management. To address the limited spatial representativeness of traditional hydrological station networks and the relatively low spatial resolution of satellite gravimetry such as the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE), this study develops a multi-source geodetic inversion framework for groundwater estimation by using Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), and GRACE satellite gravimetry. Surface deformation with high spatial resolution over the Golmud River Basin is derived from Sentinel-1 SAR images from 2017 to 2021. After correcting for modeled non-hydrological loading effects and screening observations to reduce the influence of potential non-hydrological signals, groundwater spatiotemporal variations are inverted based on elastic loading theory. The results show that from 2017 to 2021, surface deformation in the Golmud River Basin is jointly controlled by river dynamics, mineral extraction, and urbanization, forming a spatial pattern of river corridor zones and mining-related patches. Groundwater storage shows an overall increasing trend during the study period, with a particularly significant increase in the southwestern region, reaching more than 20 mm/a. A synthetic experiment demonstrates that the proposed method can recover prescribed groundwater signals at a spatial resolution of approximately 40 km under the tested conditions. Compared with the InSAR-derived estimates, GRACE-derived groundwater variations exhibit a smaller seasonal amplitude, potentially reflecting the effects of limited spatial resolution and spatial signal smoothing. The WaterGAP Global Hydrology Model (WGHM) estimates are substantially smaller in magnitude than those derived from InSAR and GRACE, highlighting the uncertainties associated with model-based groundwater estimates in this high-altitude basin. Groundwater in the Golmud River Basin experienced a rapid increase during 2017 to 2019, which is likely driven by increased precipitation and lower temperatures associated with a La Niña event, indicating a teleconnection between global climate variability and regional water resource changes. This study provides a technical reference for refined groundwater monitoring at a tens-of-kilometers scale in small and medium-scale arid basin systems.

title: Enhanced Quantitative Precipitation Estimation During Typhoon Storms Based on Optimized Dual-Polarimetric Radar Quality Control
summary: Accurate radar-based quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) plays a critical role in disaster prevention and reduction. In mountainous terrain, blockage of low-elevation radar beams can lead to missing low-level precipitation observations, while errors in specific differential phase KDP retrieval further limit QPE accuracy. To address these issues, this study uses data from two S-band dual-polarization weather radars located in Fangchenggang and Beihai, together with ground rain gauges, local raindrop size distribution (DSD) data, and digital elevation model (DEM) data. Hybrid-scan elevation construction and dual-radar mosaicking are adopted to improve the effective coverage of low-elevation observations, and a threshold-fusion strategy for KDP, denoted as KDP_TF, is proposed. The strategy selects the larger of the conventionally quality-controlled KDP_QC and variationally reconstructed KDP_VR at each valid gate. Based on the CSU-HIDRO algorithm, three QPE products, namely the quality-control QPE (QC_QPE), the variational-reconstruction QPE (VR_QPE), and the threshold-fusion QPE (TF_QPE), are generated. The precipitation events associated with Typhoon Yagi in 2024 and Typhoon Matmo in 2025 are selected for evaluation. The results indicate that TF_QPE most effectively mitigates the underestimation of 24 h accumulated precipitation. Compared with QC_QPE, the magnitude of the negative relative bias (RB) of TF_QPE is reduced, from −27.30% to −20.07% and from −16.56% to −9.78%, respectively, for the Yagi and Matmo events; the root-mean-square error (RMSE) decreases from 46.76 to 43.79 mm and from 43.27 to 43.13 mm, respectively. The hourly precipitation results further show that TF_QPE better captures the peak intensity of heavy precipitation and exhibits no evident temporal lag relative to rain gauge observations. For the heavy precipitation category, TF_QPE also yields the highest probability of detection (POD) and critical success index (CSI). These results suggest that the QPE framework developed in this study, which integrates hybrid-scan elevation construction, dual-radar mosaicking, and threshold-fusion-based KDP optimization, can improve the effective low-elevation observational coverage in mountainous terrain and mitigate the underestimation of typhoon-induced heavy precipitation in radar QPE. These results provide technical references for typhoon-related heavy-rainfall monitoring and flood early-warning as well as radar-QPE applications over coastal Guangxi.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Multi-Location ABL Wind Profiling with Minimal Instrumentation
summary: The vertical wind profile within the Atmospheric Boundary Layer (ABL) is a critical variable for a wide range of applications, including wind energy, air traffic and Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) management, pollutant dispersion, and urban air mobility. However, its accurate characterization typically requires expensive vertical-profiling LiDAR instruments, which limits the number of locations that can be simultaneously monitored. Building upon previous work in which machine-learning algorithms were trained on LiDAR data from the University of León (Spain) to reconstruct full ABL wind profiles from a single near-surface measurement, this study replaces the traditional data-driven neural network approach with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), embedding a physical constraint directly into the loss function as evaluated by automatic differentiation, and tests two such constraints under architectural control: the Ekman boundary-layer momentum balance, closed with a Monin–Obukhov eddy viscosity, and a shear-constrained formulation based on a power-law profile with an inferred exponent. With dense supervision at the target heights, neither constraint improves on an architecture-matched network without a physical term (RMSE 1.35–1.36 m/s, direction MAE 20.1–20.4∘ across all three, Kruskal–Wallis p=0.0125). In a vertical-extrapolation protocol, training with gates up to 111 m, selecting models by their skill at 140 m, and testing blind on 170–300 m, the Ekman constraint shows no detectable advantage over its own architectural control. In contrast, the shear-constrained model does, reaching 1.80±0.01 m/s speed RMSE and 27.0∘±0.3∘ direction MAE against 2.66±0.10 m/s and 34.2∘±1.8∘ for the Ekman-constrained arm and 2.61±0.12 m/s and 33.9∘±2.0∘ for the physics-free arm, which are statistically indistinguishable from one another; the shear-constrained gain is confirmed against its own architectural control (2.64±0.08 m/s, 33.0∘±1.8∘, matching the physics-free arm), ruling out the additional output as the explanation, and converts an erratic extrapolator into a stable one. The results are consistent with the benefit of embedding physics into the loss being therefore specific to the extrapolation regime and to the formulation tested, not a generic property of physics-informed learning. These findings are based on data from a single suburban site, and multi-site validation remains necessary before they can be generalized. By eliminating the need for continuous LiDAR operation after the training phase, the proposed methodology aims to enable cost-effective monitoring of multiple locations with a single instrument.

title: Assessing Spatio-Temporal Patterns and Statistical Associations of Meteorological and Agricultural Droughts in Winter Wheat Using Multi-Source Data
summary: Characterizing the spatiotemporal differences between meteorological and agricultural drought is important for drought monitoring and risk management in major grain-producing regions. However, coordinated assessment of meteorological anomalies and crop moisture responses using multi-source data remains challenging. In this study, an integrated multi-source framework was developed to jointly characterize meteorological and agricultural drought in winter wheat across six selected growing seasons in Henan Province, China. The standardized precipitation index (SPI) and vegetation water index (VWI) were used to characterize meteorological and agricultural drought, respectively. Furthermore, standard deviational ellipse analysis and center-based spatial statistics were used to characterize drought distribution, orientation, and spatial migration, while Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine statistical associations among SPI-defined drought, VWI-defined drought, and effective irrigated area. Across the selected study periods, meteorological and agricultural drought showed distinct temporal and spatial patterns. In addition, the SPI–VWI association varied with drought severity: light drought showed the strongest positive association (r = 0.64), moderate drought showed a weak negative association (r = −0.20), and severe drought showed a moderate positive association (r = 0.57). The association between total SPI- and VWI-defined drought areas was weak (r = −0.07). At the common 1-km analysis scale, VWI-defined agricultural drought maintained a more stable spatial center and major-axis orientation than SPI-defined meteorological drought, while the difference in ellipse extent was more pronounced in the earlier study periods and narrowed markedly in the later periods. Effective irrigated area showed an exploratory negative association with total VWI-defined agricultural drought area (r = −0.72, p = 0.11; n = 6); although the association did not reach conventional statistical significance, its direction identifies irrigation conditions as relevant contextual information when interpreting variations in agricultural drought. The integrated framework provides a complementary basis for jointly assessing meteorological stress and crop moisture conditions and may support drought-risk assessment and irrigation management in major winter wheat-producing regions.

title: MCI-DETR: A Multi-Level Context Interaction Transformer for Small-Object Detection in UAV Imagery
summary: Small objects in UAV imagery often exhibit weak visual representations, suffer from background clutter, and receive insufficient cross-scale feature interaction. To address these challenges, we develop MCI-DETR, a multi-level contextual interaction detector built upon RT-DETR. First, a Local-Context Modulated Interaction Module (LCMI) is designed to selectively modulate contextual features using local structural responses, thereby suppressing irrelevant background responses while expanding the effective receptive field. Second, CATM is incorporated into the high-level feature interaction stage to form a Context Interaction Module (CCIM), strengthening target-related information through spatial- and channel-domain context mapping and additive Query–Key interaction and reducing the interference of complex backgrounds with the high-level semantic representation of weak small objects. Finally, a Multi-Scale Adaptive Gated Fusion Module (MSAGF) is designed to dynamically adjust the fusion contributions of information at different scales according to the input features, while improving the quality of cross-scale feature fusion through gated coordination between local details and global context. On VisDrone2019, MCI-DETR surpasses RT-DETR by 5.2%, 4.8%, and 3.2% in mAP50, mAP50-95, and APS, respectively, demonstrating enhanced robustness for small-object recognition in cluttered aerial imagery. MCI-DETR also achieves competitive performance on UAVDT and HIT-UAV against representative detectors, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed design under different UAV scenes and imaging conditions. Overall, MCI-DETR strengthens the representation of small objects in aerial scenes and maintains reliable detection performance in the presence of cluttered backgrounds.

title: Mapping Seasonal and Persistent Surface-Current Regimes Using Long-Term HF Radar Observations and Physics-Guided Clustering
summary: Long-term high-frequency radar (HFR) observations provide a unique opportunity to examine how coastal surface currents organise into recurrent current-field configurations. This study uses the 2013–2024 HFR-Lisbon surface-current record to identify sub-inertial regimes in the Lisbon coastal region, a dynamically complex sector of the western Iberian margin. Hourly HFR currents were quality controlled, filtered with a centred 33 h rolling mean and restricted to a sub-inertial analysis domain defined from long-term coverage and residual semidiurnal-energy criteria. A physics-guided K-means clustering approach was then applied to seven physically interpretable descriptors of current intensity, directional coherence, spatial contrast, temporal change and bathymetry-based current-speed distribution. Four recurrent regimes were identified: a low-energy regime, a shelf-intensified regime, a moderate slope/offshore regime and an energetic offshore-intensified regime. The regimes show coherent spatial structures, marked seasonal organisation, persistence over several days and preferential temporal pathways. ERA5 winds, analysed a posteriori, show the strongest contrast between the low-energy regime, associated primarily with weaker-than-average winds, and the energetic offshore-intensified regime, associated with stronger and more northerly wind conditions. The results demonstrate the value of long-term HFR observations and physics-guided clustering for identifying and interpreting recurrent coastal surface-current configurations.

title: CVAC-Net: Cross-View Alignment and Adaptive Collaboration Network for Aerial–Ground Visual Tracking
summary: Aerial–ground visual tracking facilitates dynamic remote sensing and scene monitoring by integrating complementary observations from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and ground cameras, allowing one view to compensate when the target is poorly observed or temporarily invisible in the other. However, substantial cross-view variations in target appearance, scale, and geometry make it difficult to establish reliable target correspondences and effectively fuse complementary cues. To address these challenges, we propose CVAC-Net, a Cross-View Alignment and Adaptive Collaboration Network for aerial–ground visual tracking. Specifically, CVAC-Net uses cross-view contrastive learning to reduce semantic differences and a learned spatial offset to adjust the relative positions of aerial- and ground-view target features within their normalized search crops. Next, it uses the similarity between the main-view template and the aligned auxiliary-view search features to generate an importance map that reweights redundant and target-irrelevant regions, thereby improving the reliability of feature aggregation. Finally, its view-specific branches select and weight the top-K encoder outputs to integrate complementary cross-view features. Extensive experiments on the UAV–ground visual tracking (UGVT) benchmark show that CVAC-Net improves the baseline by 3.2, 3.1, and 1.7 percentage points in success rate (SR), normalized precision rate (NPR), and precision rate (PR), respectively. We further evaluate CVAC-Net using a two-dimensional (2D) single-object tracking protocol derived from Griffin using its predefined training and validation splits, providing supplementary validation on a simulated aerial–ground distribution.

title: Dual-Domain Fusion for Small-Object SAR Ship Detection in Complex Scenes
summary: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) ship detection is essential for maritime surveillance, yet coherent speckle can obscure tiny offshore vessels, while high-response coastal structures can produce target-like responses. Repeated downsampling further weakens sparse vessel signatures, whereas a separate high-resolution prediction head increases dense prediction costs. We propose a dual-domain detector that embeds spatial–frequency encoding, multiscale refinement, and high-resolution feature transfer within the backbone–neck–pyramid representation. Scharr-derived boundary cues are coupled with learned frequency context and remain discriminative as features are fused across scales, while sample-preserving space-to-depth transformation and global–local receptive-field modeling integrate shallow detail into semantically stronger P3 features without introducing a separate P2 prediction head. Coordinated FSEM, MSFE, and SOEP modules preserve fine vessel structure and reduce clutter-induced ambiguity throughout the detection hierarchy. Experiments on SSDD, HRSID, and RSDD-SAR evaluate detection accuracy, cross-dataset transfer, limited-data behavior, sensitivity to controlled perturbations, and edge deployment. Across 30 seed-matched SSDD runs, the method improves mAP50:95 over the baseline by 2.70±0.34 percentage points. It achieves 69.3% and 71.5% mAP50:95 on HRSID and RSDD. On the Atlas 200I platform, the compiled FP16 model retains 69.3% mAP50:95 while running at 101.8 frames/s.

title: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Sentinel-1 SAR Wave-Mode Significant Wave Height Retrieval via Spotter-Buoy-Corrected ERA5 Reanalysis
summary: Significant wave height (SWH) is a fundamental parameter for ocean engineering, maritime safety, and climate studies. Although spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) wave mode observations provide global, all-weather coverage, accurate SWH retrieval remains challenging due to the complex ocean-to-SAR imaging mechanism. This paper presents an explainable machine learning algorithm for retrieving SWH from Sentinel-1 SAR wave mode data. To address the scarcity of high-quality collocations and the black-box nature of existing deep-learning approaches, we first correct ERA5 SWH against high-quality Spotter drifting in situ using quantile mapping (QM). The bias-corrected ERA5 data are then collocated with Sentinel-1 SAR to generate a large-scale, globally distributed, and Spotter-calibrated training dataset. Here, QM maps each quantile of the ERA5 data distribution onto the corresponding quantile of the collocated Spotter distribution, thereby adjusting the statistical distribution of the reanalysis. An eXtreme gradient boosting regression model is then trained on 32 physically interpretable features extracted from Sentinel-1 Level-2 products, including image statistics, spectral parameters, azimuth cutoff wavelength, normalized radar cross section, and wind-related variables. Comprehensive temporal-independent validations against Spotter buoys and multi-mission altimeter data throughout one year of 2021 (excluded both from the QM correction and from model training) demonstrate high accuracy, with root-mean-square errors of 0.36 m (WV1) and 0.45 (WV2) for SAR–Spotter matchups over the range 0.5–10.0 m. In addition, SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) analysis is employed to quantify feature contributions and enhance model transparency. Furthermore, a compact 12-feature model selected via SHAP-based hierarchical clustering retains a nearly equivalent performance while improving interpretability. The proposed approach offers a reliable and transparent solution for global SAR-based SWH monitoring.

title: Cross-Scale Consistency and Scale Effects of Vegetation Phenology Across China: Evidence from MODIS Data
summary: Vegetation phenology derived from satellite vegetation indices is sensitive to spatial scale, yet how spatial aggregation affects phenological timing and temporal dynamics across broad geographical extents remains insufficiently understood. In this study, the 250 m MOD13Q1 Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) time series from 2000 to 2024 was used as a common data source, and 1 km and 5 km datasets were generated directly through spatial aggregation. By maintaining the same sensor, vegetation index, temporal sampling, and phenology retrieval method across scales, this controlled within-source framework minimizes confounding effects associated with cross-sensor differences. The start of the growing season (SOS) and end of the growing season (EOS) were retrieved using asymmetric Gaussian fitting combined with a dynamic threshold method. Their spatiotemporal patterns, aggregation-induced cross-scale consistency, and bias were systematically analyzed. The broad spatial patterns of multi-year mean SOS and EOS remained generally consistent across the three scales. SOS showed an overall advancing tendency and EOS an overall delaying tendency, while the proportion of pixels with relatively large trend magnitudes decreased at coarser spatial scales. Cross-scale correlations remained high across all scale pairs and generally increased with latitude, with SOS exhibiting higher cross-scale consistency than EOS. Annual SOS correlations declined during 2000–2024, whereas EOS correlations increased during the early part of the record and declined thereafter, with a breakpoint around 2010. The bias showed clear differences in direction and magnitude between SOS and EOS and among vegetation types, and its absolute magnitude generally increased with increasing scale disparity. These results indicate that aggregation-induced phenological responses are not spatially uniform but vary systematically with geographical context, vegetation type, and phenological phase. These findings provide a scientific reference for the cross-scale comparison and scale transformation of multi-source remotely sensed phenology products, as well as for studies of regional ecological processes.

title: UAV-LiDAR and Machine Learning for Estimating Individual Tree Diameter at Breast Height in Chinese Fir Plantations Approaching Maturity
summary: Chinese fir (Cunninghamia lanceolata) is a major plantation species in southern China, and diameter at breast height (DBH) is an essential variable for forest inventory, biomass estimation, and carbon accounting. However, direct DBH extraction from UAV-LiDAR is limited in near-mature stands because lower-stem points are often occluded by dense canopies. This study developed a UAV-LiDAR-based workflow for individual tree segmentation, structural parameter extraction, and multivariate DBH estimation in near-mature Chinese fir plantations. Field measurements were conducted in 16 sample plots. Segmentation was evaluated against a common reference set of 428 field trees across the three CHM configurations, and 412 trees with unambiguous one-to-one field-to-crown matches were retained for DBH modeling. Canopy height models (CHMs) with spatial resolutions of 0.5, 0.25, and 0.1 m were compared using watershed segmentation. For the selected 0.25 m CHM, maximum crown-polygon height (CHM_H) and equivalent-area crown diameter (CD) were extracted. CD was calculated from crown area (CA), and CA was therefore excluded from all final multivariate models to avoid deterministic redundancy. Among the tested resolution-smoothing configurations, the 0.25 m CHM yielded the highest recall, precision, and F-score values of 94.86%, 92.69%, and 93.76%, respectively. In the height-metric comparison, CHM_H achieved R2 = 0.802 and RMSE = 0.928 m, slightly outperforming H90 under the prespecified RMSE criterion. On the same holdout, classical height–crown allometry yielded R2 = 0.605, RMSE = 1.701 cm, and MAE = 1.297 cm. BPNN retained the highest reported validation R2 (0.662) and the lowest reported RMSE (1.581 cm) and was selected as the best-performing model under the study design. The workflow provides a practical basis for non-destructive DBH estimation and precision inventory in near-mature Chinese fir plantations.

title: DAMD-Net: Anisotropic Range–Doppler Feature Learning for Maritime Target Recognition
summary: Range–Doppler (RD) spectrogram-based maritime target recognition requires effective feature learning when labeled training samples are limited and the range and Doppler axes convey different physical information. We propose DAMD-Net, which combines Asymmetric Dimension-Aware Fusion (ADF) with a Dual-Directional Attention Module (DDAM). ADF integrates range-wise scattering features, Doppler-wise motion features, and local two-dimensional context, while DDAM recalibrates the fused representation through axis-specific descriptors and learnable fusion weights. With 5% of the simulated dataset used for training, DAMD-Net achieves 86.15±0.43% accuracy and 83.57±0.41% macro-F1. With 10% used for training, the corresponding results are 89.55±0.39% accuracy and 87.48±0.51% macro-F1. At the smaller 1% and 2% training budgets, DAMD-Net improves macro-F1 over VGG16 by 1.64 and 1.82 percentage points, respectively, with positive unadjusted 95% paired confidence intervals. Each training budget uses an additional 4049 labeled validation samples. Component ablations, kernel and pooling sensitivity studies, and condition-holdout evaluations examine the contribution of directional modeling; DAMD-Net has higher mean accuracy than VGG16 in all three elevation-holdout intervals. Controlled perturbation tests show advantages under partial Doppler masking and structured synthetic clutter: at a baseline-RD-to-added-clutter ratio of −10 dB, accuracy reaches 62.74%, compared with 36.68% for VGG16. On the external MTDSP dataset, DAMD-Net achieves 97.13% accuracy; on the measured LSS-DAUR dataset, it achieves 75.00±14.03% accuracy under five-fold cross-validation. DAMD-Net also reduces parameters by 89.9% and registered FLOPs by 52.6% relative to VGG16. Together, these findings support explicit RD anisotropy modeling for recognition with restricted training data, with complementary benefits in the evaluated disturbance conditions and model storage.

title: Non-Linear PSInSAR Analysis of Surface Deformation Using Sentinel-1 Data: Evaluating the Effects of Urban Expansion
summary: Surface deformation monitoring plays a crucial role in various fields, including geology, geodesy, and environmental studies. This study provides insights into the application of non-linear PSInSAR techniques for studying surface deformation associated with urban growth and groundwater pumping. A Persistent Scatterer InSAR (PSInSAR) analysis employing a time-segmented (non-linear) velocity model was applied to 119 Sentinel-1A ascending acquisitions spanning 10 February 2017 to 27 December 2020, yielding 38,594 persistent scatterers. The 33,238 scatterers were retained at a temporal coherence threshold of 0.70 and a mean density of 18.6 PS/km2 across the district, rising to 57 PS/km2 within the urban core, with annual mean line-of-sight (LOS) velocities measured for each calendar year. Temporal validation identifies a modest, origin-dependent forecasting benefit from segmentation in the urban core but no consistent advantage under contiguous block testing. Land use/land cover (LULC) was mapped from Landsat imagery for 2000, 2007, 2014, and 2020 using a random forest classifier in Google Earth Engine. LOS velocities span approximately +40 to −60 mm/yr over the mapped range, with the most negative values concentrated in the central urban core. Paired annual comparisons, accounting for spatial dependence and Holm adjustment across 15 tests, did not establish significant changes in the 0–2 km core. Significant contrasts occurred in two comparison annuli, but their physical origin remains unresolved. Land use classification maps for the years 2000, 2007, 2014, and 2020 show a significant expansion in built-up areas, coupled with a reduction in vegetation and, after adjustment for classification accuracy, in water bodies, which indicates the increasing pressure of urban growth on the environment. Lahore has witnessed a substantial increase in population due to urban migration, natural growth, and economic opportunities. Subsidence can lead to structural damage to buildings, infrastructure, and underground utilities. It is a serious concern in Lahore, particularly in areas where groundwater pumping is excessive.

title: Validation of Satellite-Derived and Reanalysis Solar Irradiance Databases Across Indonesia’s Tropical Climate Zones
summary: Accurate solar irradiance data are essential for photovoltaic (PV) resource assessment in Indonesia, yet no hourly-resolution multi-database validation exists across the archipelago scale. This study evaluates four gridded solar irradiance databases, CAMS, JAXA Himawari-9, NASA POWER, and ERA5, against quality-controlled ground measurements from 26 BMKG stations spanning all three major Köppen climate zones (Af, Am, Aw) during 2023–2024. CAMS achieved the highest hourly correspondence (median R2 = 0.855, rRMSE = 28.1%), and JAXA was close behind (R2 = 0.848), while NASA POWER showed the lowest systematic bias (rMBE = +3.6%). ERA5 showed the largest hourly errors (R2 = 0.617, rRMSE = 41.2%) consistent with its model-generated cloud fields that are unable to reproduce the localized convective-cloud variability. Because CAMS and JAXA infer cloud from the same Himawari-9 AHI observations on a common 0.05° grid, their comparison reduced sensor and resolution-related differences and focused on the retrieval design. Both showed closely comparable performance (clear-sky R2 = 0.925 vs. 0.913), and this gap widens as cloud frequency increases across the three climate zones. All four databases showed substantially larger relative errors under overcast conditions (Kt < 0.35); the temporal aggregation reduced relative error substantially, with CAMS showing the lowest error at hourly and daily scales and NASA POWER the lowest monthly rRMSE. These results provide an archipelago-scale hourly-resolution validation of four structurally distinct databases across Indonesia’s three tropical climate zones, supporting product selection and bias-correction strategies for solar resource application in Indonesia.

title: Groundwater Recovery and Land Deformation in the Beijing Plain: A Review
summary: Groundwater recovery can reduce land subsidence without immediately reversing aquifer-system compaction. This review synthesizes 101 original studies of the Beijing Plain to examine deformation during groundwater depletion and subsequent recovery. The evidence includes interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR), leveling, groundwater records, borehole deformation measurements and laboratory experiments. Historical surveys and satellite observations document expanding subsidence centers followed by widespread deceleration and localized rebound. Groundwater pressure changes are the principal regional forcing. Sedimentary architecture, hydraulic connectivity and loading history govern the magnitude and timing of deformation. Delayed pressure equilibration and time-dependent strain can sustain compaction after aquifer heads rise, while irreversible strain limits recovery of lost elevation. Surface uplift can therefore coexist with compaction at depth and does not establish restoration of aquifer-system storage capacity. Observational coverage remains uneven: 75 studies use InSAR, whereas 17 report borehole deformation measurements. Paired pressure and interval-deformation measurements are needed to identify the sources of continuing compaction. Differential ground movement remains relevant to infrastructure assessment even where regional subsidence slows.

title: Karenia brevis on the West Florida Shelf: MODIS Satellite Tracking of Bloom Dynamics Following Hurricanes Helene and Milton
summary: Karenia brevis, a harmful algal bloom (HAB) organism behind Florida’s red tide, persists in the Gulf of Mexico year-round at low concentrations. It can rapidly multiply and cause toxic outbreaks that harm marine life and human respiratory health. Red tide has been observed to suppress or intensify following tropical cyclones. Hurricanes Helene and Milton made landfall on Florida’s Gulf Coast 13 days apart in fall 2024, whereafter K. brevis proliferated along southwest Florida, with cell concentrations reaching millions of cells per liter. Remote sensing (MODIS Aqua ocean-color and sea surface temperature, 2024–2025 hurricane seasons), in situ, and hurricane best-track/reanalysis data were examined with time series analysis, statistical analysis, and spatial analysis. We found a hurricane-associated cascade within 18 days of Milton’s landfall: wind forcing, then river discharge, then chlorophyll a and K. brevis peaks, followed ~6 weeks later by another K. brevis peak within ~2% of the near-term peak in magnitude. These findings indicate that elevated wind speed and river discharge, used as a proxy for potential nutrient delivery, during and after hurricane passage are associated with a long-term K. brevis response.

title: A Training-Independent Sentinel-1/2 Phenological Approach for Interpretable Paddy Rice Mapping in Heilongjiang, China
summary: Accurate identification of paddy rice from satellite imagery is challenging in heterogeneous agricultural landscapes because water, wetland, and vigorous summer vegetation can exhibit spectral and radar responses similar to those of rice at individual observation dates. This study develops an interpretable, training-independent rice-mapping approach, meaning that the final classification does not rely on supervised classifier training, although manually interpreted locations were used for exploratory threshold selection. The approach identifies paddy fields from their characteristic transition from early-season inundation to subsequent canopy development. These phenological signals were integrated using explicit decision rules within a cropland-constrained domain, followed by persistent-water exclusion and spatial refinement. The framework was applied to the 2025 rice-growing season in the agricultural regions analyzed in Heilongjiang Province, China, using 30 m output mapping. Validation with 695 independent reference observations yielded an overall accuracy of 92.09%, Cohen’s kappa of 0.791, rice producer’s accuracy of 94.87%, user’s accuracy of 75.90%, and an F1-score of 84.33%. The high producer’s accuracy indicates effective detection of reference rice locations, whereas the lower user’s accuracy shows that commission error remains the principal limitation, particularly in areas with moisture and vegetation conditions resembling paddy fields. Sequential screening further showed that combining phenological evidence with cropland and water constraints substantially reduced the candidate mapping domain. The proposed approach provides an auditable alternative to training-dependent classification workflows and offers a transparent basis for repeatable rice mapping and agricultural monitoring, while requiring further evaluation across multiple years and regions before broader operational transfer.

title: Advanced AI-Based Techniques for Empirical Chronological Mapping of Lava Flows Using Multispectral Satellite Imagery: A Case Study of Mount Etna
summary: Effusive volcanic eruptions pose significant hazards to populated areas, making the accurate dating of lava flows essential for reconstructing eruptive histories and assessing volcanic risk. Traditional dating techniques, such as radiometric, paleomagnetic and lichenometric methods, are highly reliable but require direct sampling, complex analytical procedures, and substantial financial resources. Satellite remote sensing provides a non-invasive and spatially extensive approach that can complement conventional methods in the regional investigation of exposed volcanic surfaces. This study presents a two-stage hybrid classification–regression framework for empirical age estimation and chronological mapping of historical lava surfaces on Mount Etna, spanning the 17th to the 21st centuries. In the first stage, a Random Forest Classifier distinguishes background, pre-1600 lava surfaces, and post-1600 historical lava surfaces, thereby defining the spatial applicability domain of the chronological model. In the second stage, a Random Forest Regressor estimates age only for pixels classified as post-1600 lava by integrating ten Sentinel-2 surface-reflectance bands, elevation derived from the Digital Elevation Model (DEM), and a binary north-flank spatial indicator. On the balanced pixel-level test dataset, the RFR achieved an R2 of 0.549, a Mean Absolute Error of 66.2 years, and a Root Mean Squared Error of 89.0 years. Using the median prediction for each test eruption, the corresponding eruption-level values were R2=0.701, MAE =51.6 years, and RMSE =67.2 years. Prediction errors were larger for the oldest evaluated surfaces, indicating reduced empirical discrimination near the lower boundary of the calibrated chronological domain. This pattern may reflect calibration-boundary effects, sparse chronological coverage, eruption-specific variability, and possible convergence of surface spectral properties. Comparison with an RBF-SVR showed comparable but metric-dependent performance, without establishing the overall superiority of either regression architecture. Permutation analysis indicated that most predictive information within this dataset was associated with the Sentinel-2 spectral component, particularly the Red Edge bands. The proposed method should therefore be interpreted as a complementary fast empirical lava age-estimation and regional screening framework for exposed historical lava surfaces, rather than as a substitute for radiometric, paleomagnetic, or field-based dating.

title: Explainable XGBoost–SHAP Modeling Coupled with GeoDetector for Forest-Fire Occurrence Susceptibility and Future Climate Sensitivity in the Dabie Mountains
summary: Forest-fire occurrence susceptibility prediction remains challenging in mountainous regions because fire occurrence is controlled by nonlinear interactions among climatic, vegetation, topographic, and anthropogenic factors. Developing interpretable prediction models that integrate multi-source environmental information is essential for improving susceptibility assessment and understanding predictor contributions. Using 2003–2022 MODIS active-fire records and multi-source environmental data from the Dabie Mountains, this study developed an explainable XGBoost-based forest-fire occurrence susceptibility prediction framework. The predictive performance of XGBoost was compared with Random Forest and radial basis function support vector machine (RBF-SVM) using five-fold cross-validation, and TreeSHAP was applied to interpret predictor contributions, nonlinear responses, and interactions. KDE, standard deviational ellipses (SDEs), and GeoDetector were further used to characterize historical fire patterns and complementary spatial associations, while an independent climate-scale XGBoost model was applied to evaluate future susceptibility sensitivity under SSP126 and SSP585 scenarios. XGBoost achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.850, and log-transformed population showed the largest global SHAP contribution. GeoDetector identified precipitation and relative humidity as the strongest spatial associations with historical fire-density patterns across KDE bandwidths. The climate-scale model achieved a pooled five-fold ROC-AUC of 0.830 and indicated stronger late-century susceptibility-score redistribution under SSP585 than under SSP126. Together, these results demonstrate an explainable susceptibility modeling approach that integrates predictive modeling, model interpretation, spatial analysis, and future climate assessment. The outputs represent relative susceptibility and scenario-specific sensitivity responses rather than unconditional fire probabilities or deterministic forecasts.

title: Acquisition Realism in Virtual Terrestrial Laser Scanning of IFC Bridge Models: A Screening Study of Boundary-Aware Synthetic-to-Real Transfer for Point Cloud Segmentation
summary: Terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) of bridges supports as-built reconstruction and digital-twin maintenance, but semantic segmentation of such scans is limited by annotation cost, and synthetic point clouds generated from building information models (BIM/IFC) are the established remedy. The virtual scanner behind such data is usually a single fixed design decision validated on synthetic test splits, leaving open whether such benchmarks can be trusted and which acquisition-realism effects justify their cost. This research decomposes virtual laser scanning of four real IFC bridge models into four switchable realism factors—occlusion, incidence-angle dropout, range-dependent noise, and per-station registration error—and measures each factor’s effect, in a leave-one-factor-out screening design, on transfer to twenty real TLS bridge scans. Three findings result. (1) Synthetic-test accuracy overstates real performance by up to +5.2 mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) points: the least realistic generator scores highest on its own test split while transferring no better, and realistic acquisition drives the overstatement towards zero. (2) Boundary-aware metrics, introduced here to infrastructure point clouds, separate component-interface failures that mIoU conflates. (3) After fine-tuning on fifteen real bridges, only realism pre-training improves significantly over training from scratch (+3.6 mIoU points, Welch t(4.0) = 3.48, p = 0.025, Hedges’ g = 2.27), with a same-direction gain at component interfaces. IFC-derived and real-scan supervision are quantifiably complementary.

title: Initial Experimental Demonstration of Microwave Imaging for Mapping Leakage-Induced Subsurface Anomalies
summary: The detection and spatial assessment of buried water pipeline leaks are critical for preventing resource loss and geohazards such as soil erosion and subsidence. This paper presents an initial experimental demonstration of a microwave imaging system designed for mapping subsurface anomalies induced by buried water pipeline leaks. The proposed system integrates a custom-designed broadband open-sleeve dipole antenna with a vector network analyzer, power amplifier, and a precision linear motion stage that emulates synthetic aperture radar scanning for controlled measurement validation. The antenna achieves a 66.7% impedance bandwidth (1∼2 GHz) and a stable gain of approximately 8 dBi. A phase-compensated back-projection algorithm is employed to generate two-dimensional ground-projected scattering maps. Controlled experiments involving wet-sand regions, surface potholes, and subsurface cavity surrogates yield averaged within-image response differences of 2.1∼5.2 dB between anomaly-associated regions and ground background regions. Under the specified acquisition conditions, the theoretical azimuth and range resolutions are 0.28 m and 0.15 m, respectively. These results provide preliminary evidence of imaging feasibility under the tested surrogate-target conditions. Further validation with actual leakage and representative soil and surface-cover conditions is required to assess applicability to infrastructure monitoring.

title: Statistical Evidence for a DQN-Family Advantage in a Resource-Coupled Satellite-Ground Scheduling Benchmark
summary: Resource-coupled satellite-ground scheduling requires decisions whose computational, energy, thermal, and communication effects persist across task arrivals. We tested whether the deep Q-network (DQN) family provides a reproducible advantage over short-horizon planning in a synthetic benchmark with clipped, soft-constrained resources. Six DQN objectives used the same state representation, network architecture, replay procedure, optimizer, interaction budget, 20 model seeds, and held-out traces. Across five fully coupled regimes, every one of the 30 objective–regime comparisons had lower mean episode cost for DQN than for four-step model-predictive control (MPC-4). Every paired 95% bootstrap interval excluded zero, and all Holm-adjusted sign tests supported this ordering. The least-favorable mean difference was −5.92, with a family-wide simultaneous 95% upper bound of −5.03. Differences among DQN objectives were smaller and scenario-dependent. Additional nominal tests assessed discount-factor, training-length, greedy-rollout, and CPU decision-time sensitivity. These findings apply only to this synthetic, soft-constraint benchmark. Hard energy and thermal limits can change the feasible action set and therefore the algorithm ordering.

title: SDU-G2A: Self-Derived Uncertainty Guidance for Ground-to-Aerial Remote-Sensing Image Synthesis with Probabilistic BEV Footprints
summary: Urban planning and land-use monitoring require not only semantic land-cover maps, but also image-like overhead observations that preserve the spatial organization of urban scenes. Conventional remote-sensing segmentation and image-generation methods usually operate by obtaining available overhead imagery or in reliable overhead conditions. Street-level panoramas are easier to collect and update, but they observe the target scene from a limited terrestrial viewpoint. Recovering overhead information from a single panorama, therefore, requires inferring from an unobserved land-cover footprint before synthesizing a nadir-view remote-sensing image. We propose SDU-G2A, a two-stage framework for aerial image synthesis from a single ground panorama. Stage I predicts a probabilistic BEV land-cover footprint from the input panorama. The proposed Azimuthal-Radial Mapper propagates azimuthal evidence and applies distance-aware supervision to improve semantic recovery in occluded and far-field regions. Stage II converts the inferred footprint into a remote-sensing-like aerial image through diffusion-based synthesis, making the reconstructed urban structure available in an overhead-image form for visual interpretation and geospatial-correspondence evaluation. The main difficulty is that the inferred BEV footprint exhibits spatially varying reliability. Treating it as a deterministic condition can force cross-view segmentation errors into the generated image. SDU-G2A, therefore, derives a pixel-wise uncertainty map from Stage I predictions and uses it as a spatial reliability layer. This design preserves structures with high prediction confidence while allowing uncertain regions to be completed under text-guided and prior-driven generation. Experiments on VIGORv2 show that SDU-G2A improves BEV land-cover estimation, reduces radial prediction errors, and achieves stronger geospatial correspondence and aerial-feature distributional realism than representative G2A baselines. These results indicate that self-derived land-cover uncertainty can bridge cross-view semantic footprint inference and reliable remote-sensing image synthesis from accessible street-level observations.

title: Object-Based Reconstruction of Mining-Associated Water Body Lifecycles from Multisource Satellite Time Series
summary: Mining-associated water bodies are typically mapped as independent annual patches, obscuring their formation, transformation and continuity over time. Changes in visible water therefore need to be distinguished from changes in water body identity and surface state. Here, we develop an object-based, interval-aware framework to reconstruct water body lifecycles across seven domains in the Huainan and Huaibei coalfields, China, separating persistent identity from geometry and surface state. The framework integrates Landsat, Sentinel-2, PlanetScope and RapidEye imagery with contextual evidence to interpret changes and constrain event timing. Across these domains, the screened visible water area increased by 853.0 ha between the 2015–2017 and 2022–2024 epochs, comprising 1758.4 ha of gain and 905.4 ha of loss. The case histories documented continuity under photovoltaic cover and engineered subdivision, as well as terrestrial surface conversion with an unresolved termination status. In the examined cases, the changes in area and component overlap did not uniquely identify lifecycle events without temporal and spatial context evidence. Dense image sequences documented the early development and expansion of individual water bodies and bounded coalescence events. An independent blinded review reproduced 94.4% (17/18) of identity-relation decisions and all endpoint decisions in the original review sample. By distinguishing object continuity from visible water change, the framework complements area-based monitoring by providing evidence of water body lifecycle processes.

title: Dual Category-Guided Spatial Mamba Network for Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
summary: With the rapid development of aerospace technology, remote sensing images contain increasingly rich feature information, while large variations in object scales and imbalanced category distributions pose great challenges to remote sensing semantic segmentation. Current mainstream methods often rely on attention mechanisms for global modeling, yet they tend to over-average features, making it difficult to capture minority categories and preserve fine-grained details. To address these limitations, we propose a Dual Category-Guided Spatial Mamba Network (DGSMNet) that combines dual category guidance with a spatial Mamba mechanism. Specifically, a Dual-Stage Category Guidance (DSCG) module is designed to extract class information via wavelet transforms and guide feature learning, ensuring proportional representation of all categories across channels and enabling the model to learn underrepresented classes. In addition, a Spatial Mamba (SPM) module is introduced to enhance long-range modeling while retaining sensitivity to local details. By integrating DSCG and SPM, the proposed DGSMNet improves category-aware representation and spatial modeling on the evaluated benchmarks. Extensive experiments on the ISPRS Vaihingen and Potsdam datasets demonstrate that DGSMNet achieves competitive performance among the compared methods.

title: Robust Satellite Techniques for Detecting and Monitoring Icebergs by Sentinel-2 Data
summary: In recent decades, the sharp rise in global temperatures has accelerated the melting of the polar ice caps, causing icebergs to break off and subsequently drift across the sea surface. At the same time, the increase in navigable areas in the Arctic region has led to a continued growth in maritime traffic at higher latitudes, resulting in a consequent increase in the risk of iceberg–ship collisions. In this context, it is particularly important to provide vessels at sea with timely and up-to-date information on the presence of icebergs along routes in mid- and high-latitude waters. Given this challenge, this paper presents, for the first time, the Robust Satellite Techniques (RST) methodology employed at the global level to perform iceberg detection using imagery acquired only in the B3 band (centred at 560 nm) by the Sentinel-2 (S2) constellation. A test performed near Greenland (in September 2016) and in the Labrador Sea (in August 2021), showed that, in comparison with traditional fixed-threshold methods, this approach (easily implementable in the Google Earth Engine cloud platform) demonstrated: (a) very high sensitivity by doubling the number of detected icebergs (including the smaller ones); (b) high reliability with an overall false positive below 20% that becomes zero when other objects that may pose a hazard to navigation (e.g., dark ships, shallow reefs, etc.) are also considered.

title: Kernel-Driven Model Correction of Thermal Directionality: Pixel-Level Analysis Using Airborne Multi-Angular Observations
summary: Directional anisotropy (DA) in thermal infrared (TIR) remote sensing introduces significant variability in land surface temperature (LST) retrievals, particularly in high-resolution observations. This study presents the empirical pixel-level modelling of DA, by using multi-angular airborne data from the NETSense campaign over an agricultural area near Grosseto, Italy. Six kernel-driven models (KDMs) are evaluated for their ability to fit directional effects, with the Vinnikov–Roujean–Lagouarde (Vinnikov–RL) model achieving the highest accuracy (RMSE = 1.07 K). At 40 m resolution, modelled directional effects reach median deviations of +1.80 K at the hotspot position, −2.03 K opposite to the Sun, and −1.37 K perpendicular to the solar principal plane, with extremes up to ±6 K, highlighting their operational significance for missions such as LSTM, TRISHNA, and SBG. To improve operational feasibility, two simplified models—adapted RL (RLa) and Vinnikov–RLa—are introduced, leveraging a consistent inverse relationship between hotspot magnitude and width to reduce parameter complexity via a power-law formulation. The analysis reveals that directional effects vary with spatial resolution and are influenced by canopy structure and solar geometry, while biophysical parameters alone are insufficient for coefficient estimation. Validation using an independent flight day confirms the robustness of the simplified models under different acquisition geometries, surface types, and geophysical conditions. A tiered model strategy is proposed for future satellite missions, recommending model selection based on day or night observations and data availability. These findings support the integration of directional correction into operational pipelines, enabling consistent and accurate LST products across platforms, resolutions, and observation conditions.

title: Migratory Bird Identification and Density Prediction Based on Weather Radar Products and Weather Forecast Information
summary: Bird activity levels present an increasing trend in China. Bird strike risks for the aviation industry are positively correlated with bird activity. Migratory birds pose greater threats to airplanes due to their broader distribution and larger mass. A reliable broad-area surveillance solution for migratory birds is critical for bird strike warning and prevention. This paper introduces a broad-area migratory bird identification model based on weather radar systems. A customized feature space and a sample-separation optimization strategy are proposed for more accurate identification of bird targets in weather radar resolution volumes. A new bird density calculation model is proposed to accommodate nonuniform bird distributions and provide a more reasonable bird quantity interpretation. The relevance between bird density and weather parameters is modeled by specific data sampling and a numerical regression model. Weather radar data files from two stations in China are used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Results indicate that the bird identification model could provide reasonable bird surveillance information, and the density prediction models present good consistency with existing datasets. Differences among radar stations and seasons prove the necessity of building individual bird density prediction models. Identification and prediction models are expected to be further optimized with more data support and cross-validation information. Quantitative and qualitative prediction products provide valuable references for bird strike prediction and prevention.

title: Multi-Source Remote Sensing for Mangrove Mapping in South China: Sensor-Configuration Responses and Cross-Regional Model Applicability
summary: Mangrove mapping increasingly integrates multisource remote sensing, yet the geographically transferable value of additional sensors remains uncertain. This study evaluated Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, Sentinel-1 and GF-3 SAR, GF-5 AHSI hyperspectral observations, terrain variables, and sensor-independent coastal-context information across five coastal regions of southern China. Five nested feature configurations (D1–D5) were tested with Random Forest, XGBoost, DeepLabV3, and SegFormer under true leave-one-study-area-out validation on 349,898 common 10 m coordinates; deep models were replicated across three random seeds. Model-averaged F1-scores were 0.9025, 0.9031, 0.9123, 0.9134, and 0.9220 for D1–D5, respectively, but differences were not statistically supported across held-out regions (Friedman χ2 = 0.48, p = 0.9754). Sentinel-1, GF-3, and their interaction showed small, geographically inconsistent contrasts. GF-5 effects were model- and preprocessing-dependent, and cross-scene normalization altered performance in contrasting directions. Gain and grouped-permutation analyses indicated model-specific predictor use and sensitivity rather than independent sensor contribution. Overall, multisource benefits depended on sensor configuration, model representation, geographic domain, and preprocessing conditions, supporting context-specific sensor selection and geographically independent validation.

title: Systematic Divergence Between NDVI-Based and Energy-Balance Water-Stress Classifications in Sparse Hyper-Arid Olive Orchards: A Two-Decade Landsat–METRIC Evaporative CWSI Assessment
summary: Water stress in olive orchards is often mapped from the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), although in sparse orchards NDVI also reflects fractional cover and bare soil. We compared an NDVI-based classification with a METRIC-derived evaporative Crop Water Stress Index (CWSIET=1−ETa/ETo) over hyper-arid, groundwater-irrigated olive orchards of La Yarada–Los Palos (Peru), using Landsat 5/8/9 imagery from eighteen austral summers (2006–2026). Both classifications rely on operational thresholds that were not physiologically calibrated for olive: the NDVI ranges were defined from field-observed canopy condition, and the CWSIET classes are equal-width bins of the reference-normalized evaporative deficit. NDVI placed most of the cropland in severe-to-extreme classes and CWSIET mainly in mild-to-moderate classes (medians 0.26–0.41); NDVI was more severe over 89% of the cropland. The divergence grew as cover decreased, persisted at native thermal resolution and was reproduced by surface temperature, although both continuous indices correlated (r=−0.61). Without in situ physiological or flux measurements, these results establish a disagreement between indicators, not which of them matches plant water status. The cropland expanded fourfold (98 to 356 km2) with no trend in mean evapotranspiration or CWSIET. NDVI-based stress maps should be interpreted with caution in sparse orchards and combined with energy-balance, meteorological or field information.

title: Methodology for assessing the accuracy of long-term, annual land cover monitoring at national scale: Experiences from the Land Change Monitoring, Assessment, and Projection (LCMAP) initiative
summary: Annual land cover monitoring using medium-resolution satellite imagery represents a transition from periodic mapping campaigns to continuous observation systems. This transition introduces accuracy assessment challenges not encountered in one-time mapping efforts, particularly when the initial monitoring period is extended forward in time. These challenges are not addressed in existing guidance, which remains largely framed around the evaluation of maps of a single date or maps showing changes between two dates. We present a set of methodological adaptations to adjust to this evolving paradigm, using as a case study the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Land Change Monitoring, Assessment, and Projection (LCMAP) initiative, which generated annual land cover and land cover change products across the historical Landsat archive. Assessing the accuracy of these products was an essential component of LCMAP and resulted in an extensive reference sample dataset that may be used for accuracy estimation, area estimation, or support in the development of new algorithms or models. We review the LCMAP methodology and highlight challenges encountered and lessons learned that are transferable to other long-term, temporally dense monitoring programs. This framework demonstrates that statistically rigorous assessment can scale to operational annual land cover production, while the experiences of the project clarify where existing good practice guidance should be extended to support the needs of ongoing, continuous land cover monitoring.

title: A semi-empirical BPDF model for improving characterization of polarimetric reflection of land surfaces: Validation using laboratory and POLDER polarization data
summary: Bidirectional Polarization Distribution Function (BPDF) models, widely used to characterize the polarimetric properties of light reflected from targets, are crucial for linking polarization with land surface structural parameters and understanding surface contributions to polarization in radiative transfer. However, existing BPDF models face challenges in accurately representing variations in both the magnitude and distribution of polarimetric reflection across surfaces with varying structural characteristics. In this study, a three-parameter BPDF model (GMF model), which can effectively characterize polarimetric reflection of surfaces ranging from smooth to rough, was developed by combining the GGX distribution function with the Fresnel equation and a shadowing function. Multi-angular polarimetric data from laboratory measurements over three plant samples and from Polarization and Directionality of the Earth's Reflectances (POLDER) satellite observations over various land surfaces, each exhibiting distinct polarimetric reflection properties, were used to validate the proposed model. Compared with five existing models, the new model achieved the highest accuracy in simulating polarimetric reflection, reducing the overall RMSE by 33%–68% for laboratory samples and by 8%–30% for POLDER observations. This improvement is attributed to the incorporation of the GGX distribution function, which enables the new polarization model to accurately characterize the polarimetric properties of surfaces with varying structures, including sharp specular peaks over smooth surfaces and broad angular distributions over rough surfaces. Furthermore, the analysis of the model's response to parameter variations demonstrated that the GGX distribution function enhanced the ability of the GMF model to modulate the magnitude and distribution of polarimetric reflection induced by surface structure variations. The proposed polarization model is expected to advance polarized remote sensing applications in land surface monitoring.
